commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Remove per-load completeness checks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Remove the per-load completeness checks, MTP and others. Part of #54477.

> This PR reuses an old number. Its earlier content (a generic direct reload path for layerwise reload) was superseded by the direct reload that has since merged, and is gone from the diff.

Each check ran on one `load_weights` call, so it could not tell one bucket of an update from a bad checkpoint. Engines turned it off with `disable_mtp_completeness_check`, and models without that flag raised on a partial bucket.

## Changes

- Delete `mtp_validation.py`, its test, the flag handling in the IPC, M2N and NCCL engines, and the per-call checks in the draft loaders: DeepSeek family, glm5next, kimi_k3, bailing (with v3), minimax_m3, step3p5, step5, inkling, hy_v4, qwen3_dspark, muse_spark, lilicorr, llama_eagle3, qwen3_eagle3, qwen3_xpress.
- Stop deleting `confidence_head` when a load does not contain it (gemma4_dspark, qwen3_dspark, deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41). The config alone decides whether it exists, as in Kimi K3 and Muse Spark. The `deepseek-ai` V4-Pro-DSpark, V4-Flash-DSpark, V4.1-Flash, dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 and dspark_gemma4_12b_block7 checkpoints all ship it.
- Delete the same kind of check outside the draft loaders: AliceAI target weights, the Nemotron audio tower, Parse 3.5 RADIO LayerScale, MuseSpark Quark experts, the dots3 FP8 indexer pair, and the `AutoWeightsLoader` tied-alias check.
- Keep the Step5 fused qkv+indexer shard check on cold start. It asks `weight_update_active` too, so it skips updates. The Step5 MTP check for other missing parameters is removed.
- Keep the choices that depend on what the whole checkpoint contains in `load_weights`. They now ask `weight_update_active()`, a process-wide flag that `start_reload` sets and `finish_reload` clears, because one call during an update may hold only part of the checkpoint. A module nested in the model being updated, such as `Step5ForCausalLM` inside `Step5ForConditionalGeneration`, sees it too:
  - `has_own_embed_tokens = False` (minimax_m3)

## Behavior change

These stop raising, deliberately:

- A quantized checkpoint missing some or all draft weights, or a loader that returns `None`, leaves those weights at their initial values. Expect a low acceptance rate rather than an error.
- A reduced-vocabulary DSpark checkpoint missing `d2t` gets a wrong draft id mapping.
- A direct update that leaves out weights is not caught.

- A quantized checkpoint missing main-model or encoder weights (AliceAI, Nemotron audio, MuseSpark Quark, dots3) leaves them at their initial values. The main model output is wrong, not only the draft.
- A quantized checkpoint with tied embeddings that ships only the alias, such as `lm_head.weight`, leaves the shared embedding at its initial values.
- Parse 3.5 reports every RADIO LayerScale parameter as loaded, for any encoder.
- A DSpark checkpoint that lacks `confidence_head` while its config enables it, which is the DeepSeek default, raises in `track_weights_loading` if unquantized and otherwise runs with an uninitialized head.
- `reload_weights` from a checkpoint no longer runs the Step5 shard check.
- A dots3 FP8 update that splits a weight and its scale across `load_weights` calls drops both, so `wk` keeps its old value.

`track_weights_loading` still raises on an unquantized checkpoint for a missing parameter in a module with no `quant_method`, such as an MTP layer norm or a tied embedding. It exempts whole modules that have one, so missing linear weights do not raise. A follow-up adds one check by checkpoint name for direct updates and one cold-start check for drafts with no layer weights.

## Test Plan

On NV GB200 with the `nightly-1648fefab9` image (23833 used `nightly-4fab5a0747`). Each row names the commit it ran on.

| Test | Commit | Job | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit selection (21 files plus touched tests) | `8b839c0e28` | 24049 | 52 failed, 677 passed, 46 skipped |
| Same selection on main | `204e2ece5f` (main) | 24024 | 52 failed, 688 passed, 46 skipped |
| `test_load_plan.py`, `test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py`, `test_reload_lifecycle.py` in one process | `8b839c0e28` | 24048 | 80 passed |
| Qwen3.8 + MTP, trainer shape, sleep level 2, 3 direct updates | `8d5f828398` | 24025 | GSM8K 0.9598→0.9583, acceptance 0.718→0.718, 0 tracebacks |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark with draft updates and adaptive verification, same shape | `8d5f828398` | 24029 | GSM8K 5-shot 0.9484→0.9439, 40-shot 0.9533→0.9500, acceptance 0.452→0.450, 0 tracebacks |
| Step5 + MTP (Step-5-Preview), TP8 over 2 nodes, same shape | `fc6878bc9d` | 24036 | Cold start passes the shard check; GSM8K 5-shot 0.9280→0.9378, 40-shot 0.9200→0.9200, 0 tracebacks |
| GLM-5.3-Flash + MTP with draft updates, same shape | `8b839c0e28` | 24122 | GSM8K 5-shot 0.9121→0.9166, 40-shot 0.9267→0.9267, acceptance 0.804→0.803, 0 tracebacks |
| Kimi-K3 + Kimi-K3-DSpark with draft updates, TP16 over 4 nodes, same shape | `8b839c0e28` | 24111 | GSM8K 0.9515→0.9515, acceptance 0.525→0.525, 0 tracebacks |
| Step5 + MTP on main, same shape | `204e2ece5f` (main) | 24033 | GSM8K 5-shot 0.9340→0.9310, 40-shot 0.9233→0.9333 |
| Cold start of unquantized Qwen3.8 with the MTP layers removed | `f52c6c98cd` | 23833 | Raises `Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint` (`track_weights_loading`) |

The 52 failures are the same tests on this branch and on main: 46 in `test_eagle.py` (gated repo access in this environment), 2 in `test_weight_transfer_m2n.py` and 4 in `test_gemma.py`. The branch collects 11 fewer tests because it deletes tests of removed checks. `ruff` passes. `tests/distributed/test_eplb_spec_decode.py` is excluded because it hung in an earlier run (23746).

Not run: MiniMax M3 + MTP (no public checkpoint ships the `model.mtp.*` weights; unit tests cover `has_own_embed_tokens`); layerwise updates on full models; full models for AliceAI, Nemotron audio, Parse 3.5, MuseSpark Quark and dots3 (unit tests only where they exist); other MTP architectures; IPC and M2N on full models; a quantized checkpoint with missing draft weights.

commits.pr_title: [Misc] Bump ruff to v0.17.2 and enable UP032, UP042, B007, F403 and F405
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump ruff in pre-commit from v0.14.0 to v0.17.2 one minor at a time, and enable UP032, UP042, B007, F403 and F405, which were ignored until now.

## Claims

- Each bump has its own commit with the fixes it needs: the v0.15 formatter style, ISC004 (v0.16), and removing `noqa` comments that v0.15 and v0.17 made redundant.
- `ruff-format` stays off Markdown (`types_or: [python, pyi, jupyter]`), because v0.16's hook now formats Markdown code blocks and turns `--8<--` snippets into `--8 < --`.
- UP042 converts 21 `(str, Enum)` classes to `StrEnum`. After an audit, the only text that changes is in error and log messages (e.g. `AttentionType.DECODER` becomes `decoder`). No hash, metric label, payload or test assertion is affected.
- Fixes `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/__init__.py`, which listed 12 undefined names in `__all__` (so `from ...mhc import *` raised), and two `SIMPLE_PROMPT`s in the `test_accuracy.py` files that were accidentally 1-tuples.

## Validation

`pre-commit run --all-files` passes on ruff v0.17.2. mypy passes, apart from `cuda_checkpoint_executor.py` errors that also occur on `main`.

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
.venv/bin/python -m pytest <each touched test file> -q
```

I ran all 109 touched test files on macOS (CPU only). 56 pass. Every failure was checked: each one also happens on the merge base, or comes from the environment (no CUDA, `ray`/`lm_eval` not installed, no `/dev/shm`). CI covers the CUDA-only paths (mhc kernels, machete generator).

commits.pr_title: [Sleep] Warn when level-2 sleep discards draft weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This change adds a warning for level-2 sleep. The warning shows when level-2 sleep discards the private weights of the draft model and `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` does not keep them. Related: #52479, #61046. ## Claims - vLLM logs the warning one time. The warning gives the flag `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*'`. - vLLM does not log the warning in these conditions: - There is no draft model. - The draft model uses only parameters of the target model. - A pattern in `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` selects a draft parameter. - The change does not change how vLLM operates. The defaults, the memory use, and the wake-up procedure stay the same. - The change adds 11 lines to `Worker.sleep` and 3 lines to the documentation. ## Validation Test equipment: - GPU: 1× H100-80GB. - vLLM: nightly `0.33.0rc1.dev910+g4fab5a074`. - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, with the EAGLE3 draft model `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` and `num_speculative_tokens=3`. - Server flags: `--enable-sleep-mode`, with `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`. Test procedure (from #52479): 1. Send 8 greedy prompts (256 tokens each, batch size 1). 2. Send `POST /sleep?level=2`. 3. Send `POST /wake_up?tags=weights`. 4. Send `POST /collective_rpc` with `{"method": "reload_weights"}`. 5. Send `POST /wake_up?tags=kv_cache`. 6. Send the same 8 prompts again. 7. Compare the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters from step 1 and step 6. Results (one run for each row): | Build | `draft.*` | Accepted / draft tokens after wake-up (before sleep: 1218 / 2484) | Decode tok/s, before → after | Warning | |---|---|---|---|---| | base | off | **0 / 6120** | 319.4 → **131.4** | no | | base | on | 1218 / 2484 | 318.7 → 318.6 | no | | this PR | off | 0 / 6120 | 308.1 → 126.7 | **yes** | | this PR | on | 1218 / 2484 | 308.2 → 308.5 | no | | this PR, no speculative decoding | — | — | correct output after wake-up | no | In all speculative decoding rows, the greedy outputs before sleep and after wake-up are the same. The log shows this warning: ``` WARNING [gpu_worker.py:348] Level 2 sleep discards draft model weights; reload_weights restores only the target. Unless the draft is updated separately, set --sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*' to keep them. ``` The existing unit tests pass: ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k sleep # 3 passed ``` This change does not add a unit test, because it changes only the log. The change uses `_get_sleep_parameters` to find the draft parameters. The existing `test_sleep_preservation_*` tests already examine this function. If the reviewers want a unit test, I can add one. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass on the changed files. ## Details **Root cause.** Level-2 sleep discards the weights of the target model and the draft model. `reload_weights` loads only the weights of the target model. Thus, the draft model operates with incorrect weights. The verification step rejects all draft tokens, so the output stays correct. But decode speed decreases to the speed without speculative decoding. No error occurs, and the log shows no message. We found this problem when we restored vLLM replicas from level-2 sleep snapshots for autoscaling (llm-d/llm-d-autoscaling#1588). **Why a warning, and not a new default.** A `draft.*` default would increase the host memory for all speculative decoding deployments that use sleep. Also, setups that update the draft weights separately would need a flag to disable the default. A warning does not have these costs. **Design.** The check uses only the configured patterns. It does not use the saved parameter copies. Thus, the check also operates with #66010. The check runs only during level-2 sleep. It does not run during inference.
Related PRs - #52487 loads the draft weights again from disk. - #60139 adds an RPC that loads a new draft checkpoint. - #61046 added `draft.*` retention. - #66010 changes what level-2 sleep discards. Draft parameters stay discardable by default. These PRs do not add a warning. This PR does not change their behavior.
---

commits.pr_title: [Kimi-K3] Keep the latent-MoE tail fusion under sleep mode
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#64583 turned off the Kimi-K3 latent-MoE tail fusion whenever sleep mode is on, and logged a warning. At the time, level-2 sleep discarded the whole `weights` pool. The fusion's collective kernel keeps its state in that pool: the Lamport flags (`_routed_flags`, `_shared_flags`) and the peer pointer table. None of these are parameters, so they were lost on wake.

Since #66010, level 2 discards only allocations that hold nothing but parameters, and offloads and restores everything else at the same address. That state now survives sleep, so this PR removes the fallback and its warning. The tail fusion now runs with sleep mode on, at TP 8 and 16 on SM100.

- `latent_moe_runner.py`: delete the sleep-mode fallback (11 lines).
- `test_latent_moe_tail.py`: delete `test_sleep_mode_falls_back_to_default_path` and the `enable_sleep_mode` parameter that only it used.

## Test Plan

Kimi-K3 at TP 8 across two GB200 nodes (multi-node NVLink), with dummy weights and 4 layers (`hf_overrides`), CUDA graphs on, `enable_sleep_mode=True` and `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]`. Keeping every parameter means that any difference after wake comes from non-parameter state.

The run checks each rank's `LatentMoERunner`s through `collective_rpc`, then generates greedily for 16 prompts and 48 tokens:
- before sleep, twice;
- after `sleep(1)` + `wake_up()`;
- after each of two `sleep(2)` + `wake_up(["weights"])` + `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` cycles.

Each output is compared with the first, token for token.

Negative control: the same run, but after the first level-2 wake the collective kernel's Lamport flags are zeroed. This emulates what the old level 2 did to them.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py` also runs on GB200.

## Test Result

| Run | Tail fusion on (runners per rank) | Repeat | After L1 | After L2 #1 | After L2 #2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| This PR | 3 / 3 on all 8 ranks, fused path taken | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| Negative control (flags zeroed after L2 #1) | 3 / 3 on all 8 ranks | | | hangs: `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` | |

The control shows that the test catches lost tail-fusion state. Without #66010 (main at 2ced9ceb97 with the same fallback removed), the same run crashes at the first level-2 wake with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`, even though the fusion was not confirmed to be on there.

`test_latent_moe_tail.py`: 1 passed, 3 skipped (the skipped kernel tests need more GPUs).

Not covered: real Kimi-K3 weights and GSM8K (no checkpoint available here), TP 16, and level 2 with a real weight update. In that path, parameters are discarded and rewritten. That is the generic #66010 path, which this PR doesn't change.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DCP] Up-project the MLA decode output before the A2A merge
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, MLA decode all-to-alls each rank's partial latent output and applies `W_UV` after the LSE merge. This PR applies it to all DCP-gathered heads first, so the all-to-all carries 130 instead of 514 bf16 values per head (Kimi-K3, 512/128). The merge is linear per head, so only rounding changes.

## Claims

- `MLADCPManager.v_up_proj_combine` is set only for the NCCL all-to-all without PCP; symmetric-memory and `ag_rs` paths are unchanged.
- `MLAAttention` and Kimi-K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention` (also the DSpark draft's) use it when `W_UV` is unquantized. On by default.
- Cost per MLA layer: the gathered `W_UV` (+12 MiB for Kimi-K3 at TP8/DCP8, 0.32 GiB per GPU; the local `W_UV` is a view of `kv_b_proj` and adds nothing) and a BMM over N times the heads. Below 8 decode tokens that BMM costs more than the all-to-all saves, so it merges first there.
- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, TP8/DCP8, decode-bound C16 / C32: throughput +0.6% / +1.1%, 90th-percentile interactivity +1.4% / +2.8%. Decode step -1.1% / -1.7% at 24 / 32 running requests. Prefill-bound C72: interactivity +4%, throughput flat.

## Validation

- Measured here: a new 2-rank test against merge-then-project passes on MI355X, fails with a wrong head order, and runs in the Distributed Features CI steps.
- Measured here: per-layer microbenchmark, 8x MI355X, 96 or 64 heads, cold weights: project-then-merge is +1.1 µs (+4-5%) at 1-4 tokens, even at 8, and -12% to -48% from 16 to 360 tokens.
- Measured here: selection asserts pass; an 8-rank simulation at Kimi-K3 shapes gives both orders the same fp64 relative error, 2.30e-3. pre-commit clean.
- Not from this branch: end-to-end numbers (runtime patch, same math, nightly `3966924d`); GSM8K 0.958 at C32 (both orders), 0.963 at C72.

<details><summary>Tests, numeric check, end-to-end setup and numbers</summary>

Tests, on MI355X with the `3966924d` image and this branch's files overlaid:

```
$ pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k v_up_proj
4 passed, 31 deselected
```

The `v_up_proj_combine` asserts sit in the three `MLADCPManager` selection tests of `test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py`. Each of the two files has 7 failures that are identical on the unmodified image (an fp32 LSE compared with a bf16 reference in `return_lse` cases, CUDA-only direct ops); `test_dcp_a2a.py` is not in CI today, hence `-k v_up_proj`.

Numeric check. One process simulates 8 DCP ranks with the real pack and unpack-combine Triton kernels: 96 gathered heads, 12 per rank, L=512, V=128, bf16, 5 query tokens per request; the first request has KV on rank 0 only and NaN partial output elsewhere. Error of the merged output against an fp64 merge-then-project reference, as Frobenius relative error / largest element error (output RMS 0.66 to 0.70):

| Requests | Merge then project | Project then merge | Largest difference between the two |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2.19e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.19e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 1.56e-2 |
| 24 | 2.29e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.29e-3 / 1.90e-2 | 1.56e-2 |
| 32 | 2.30e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.30e-3 / 2.02e-2 | 3.13e-2 |
| 48 | 2.32e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.32e-3 / 2.65e-2 | 3.13e-2 |

All-to-all payload per rank per layer at 160 tokens: 15.8 MB before, 4.0 MB after (computed).

End-to-end setup (not run from this branch). Kimi-K3 1P1D prefill/decode disaggregation on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8 per role, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` with `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0`, FP8 KV cache, DSpark speculative decoding with 4 draft tokens, Mooncake RDMA, agentic multi-turn trace. vLLM ROCm nightly `3966924d` with `MLAAttention` and Kimi-K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention` patched at runtime to project before the merge.

| Concurrency | Projection | Total tok/s/GPU | P90 interactivity | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C16 | before merge | 5,257.4 | 108.0 | - |
| C16 | after merge (control) | 5,227.0 | 106.5 | - |
| C32 | before merge | 10,492.2 | 75.8 | 0.958 |
| C32 | after merge (control) | 10,379.9 | 73.7 | 0.958 |
| C72 | after merge | flat, see below | 38.2 | - |
| C72 | before merge | flat, see below | 39.8 | 0.963 |

Token-weighted inter-token latency: 8.3 to 8.2 ms at C16, 11.1 to 10.9 ms at C32. The control runs used different node pairs from the before-merge runs. C72 is prefill-bound; total throughput was 15,909 and 15,831 tok/s/GPU across the two runs.

Decode-only A/B on one MI355X node at a C48-like batch: decode step 46.5 to 46.0 ms at 24 running requests, 53.9 to 53.0 ms at 32.

</details>

## Details

On by default: a2a is opt-in or model-selected, and CUDA with DCP symmetric memory keeps its direct combine. Both orders round twice to the activation dtype.

Limitations: not run on CUDA, or end to end from this branch; the 8-token threshold is measured on MI355X only. DeepSeek-V3.2 attention and direct symmetric-memory A2A keep merge-then-project.

Related: #48196 (draft, conflicting) puts the same projection, for every DCP backend, in a larger sparse-MLA change predating `MLADCPManager`. AI-assisted (Claude in Cursor).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Emit the o_proj MXFP8 input from the NVFP4 sparse decode kernel
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose On ROCm, every MiniMax-M3.1 decode layer runs the NVFP4 sparse decode attention, then a separate `_kernel` launch (the MXFP8 activation quant of its bf16 output, K = 2048 per TP4 rank), then the `o_proj` GEMM. In the profile of a real decode step (rank-0 profile windows at N=4 and N=16) that quant is 60 launches per step, ~4.4-4.6 us each (profiled, inflated ~1.6x). This PR adds an `fp8_out` variant of the FlyDSL sparse decode kernel (`m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode_*_q8`) whose final store writes E4M3 values and row-major E8M0 scales instead of bf16, and hands them to `o_proj` as a `QuantizedActivation` (same mechanism as #63637 for `qkv_proj` and the FFN fusion in #65478). ## How it works - Output layout: in the final store a lane owns head `n`, dims `32g..32g+31`, i.e. exactly one 32-element MX block, so the quantization needs no cross-lane exchange. With split-K (`splits > 1`) the last workgroup of a row merges the partials and stores O; the quant runs there on the merged O, so every 32-block sees the final values. - Arithmetic: it quantizes the *bf16-rounded* values the bf16 store would have written (`pk_bf16`), computes the block amax on their integer bit patterns and the E8M0 byte as `clamp(exponent_field - 8 + (mantissa > 0.75), 0, 254)` (448 = 1.75 x 2^8, so this is `ceil(log2(amax/448)) + 127` exactly, no log2/division), scales by the exact power of two `2^(127-sb)` and converts with `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32` (RNE). Hence the output is bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the same kernel's bf16 output (not "more accurate": it is the same values, unlike the swiglu fusion in #65478). - The scale formula was checked on CPU against `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch` on 20,000 random bf16 blocks over ~2^60 dynamic range plus edge blocks (zeros, subnormals, 447/448/449, the 1.75 boundary and the value just above it): 0 mismatches. The whole kernel compiles for gfx950 for splits 1/4/8 (`FLYDSL` compile-only on CPU). Bit-exactness on MI355X: see Tests. - Gating: `fp8_out` is a compile-time variant; the bf16 kernel and all other callers are unchanged. Both assert bitwise equality of values and scales with `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the bf16 kernel output and that rows past the batch are untouched. Result: the 96 new tests pass, and the whole file passes (176 passed), i.e. the existing decode tests are unchanged. The `i8` scale store and the split-merge path were correct on the first run. ## Measurements Profile trace Before: After: Graph-replay microbenchmark (a small benchmark script; 200 back-to-back launches per graph, median of 15 replays; 8 rows per request, 16 heads per rank, MI355X, 1 GPU), us per launch. "bf16 + quant" is the current path (decode kernel then `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`). Context 150K: | N | bf16 kernel | bf16 + separate quant | MXFP8 epilogue kernel | saved | epilogue cost vs bf16 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 10.34 | 12.56 | 10.57 | 1.99 | +0.24 | | 2 | 10.74 | 12.78 | 10.93 | 1.85 | +0.19 | | 3 | 10.82 | 12.91 | 11.02 | 1.89 | +0.20 | | 4 | 10.86 | 12.99 | 11.14 | 1.85 | +0.28 | | 5 | 11.56 | 13.66 | 11.90 | 1.77 | +0.34 | | 6 | 10.07 | 12.15 | 10.29 | 1.87 | +0.22 | | 8 | 10.27 | 12.39 | 10.48 | 1.91 | +0.21 | | 12 | 13.67 | 15.91 | 14.13 | 1.78 | +0.46 | | 16 | 13.84 | 16.09 | 14.31 | 1.78 | +0.47 | | 24 | 18.39 | 20.72 | 18.64 | 2.09 | +0.25 | 30K and 500K contexts give the same numbers within 0.1 us (saved 1.79-2.11 us at 30K, 1.81-2.04 us at 500K). The separate quant costs about 2.2 us in the graph; the epilogue adds 0.2-0.5 us to the attention kernel, so the net saving is 1.8-2.1 us per layer. ## End to end (MI355X, TP4, DSpark 7 drafts, 150K context, DBO off, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0`) Arms on the same installed tree, 5 repeats each: **S0** = a tree that already contains the FFN quant fusions of #65478 and the routed-scale fold (so the baseline already has the other launch removals), **S2** = S0 + this PR; S0 was also run again at the end to check drift (S0 start and end agree within 0.14 ms at every N). **Profile window (rank 0, 60 steps, all streams), N=4 and N=16:** `_kernel.kd` (the MXFP8 activation quant) **82 -> 22 per decode step**, total kernels per step **1399 -> 1339 (N=4) and 1456 -> 1396 (N=16)**: exactly the 60 launches this PR removes; nothing else changes. **Decode step p50 (ms), median of 5 repeats** (noise of this benchmark about +-0.1-0.2 ms): | N | S0 start | S0 end | S2 (this PR) | vs mean(S0) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 9.10 | 9.13 | 9.09 | -0.3% | | 2 | 10.04 | 10.05 | 10.00 | -0.4% | | 3 | 11.28 | 11.31 | 11.25 | -0.4% | | 4 | 11.65 | 11.53 | 11.66 | +0.6% | | 5 | 12.71 | 12.71 | 12.56 | -1.2% | | 6 | 13.08 | 13.10 | 13.13 | +0.3% | | 8 | 14.41 | 14.36 | 14.30 | -0.6% | | 12 | 16.01 | 16.15 | 15.85 | -1.4% | | 16 | 18.05 | 18.08 | 18.04 | -0.1% | The step-level change is small: negative at 7 of 9 batch sizes, mean -0.4% (about 0.05 ms), average -0.8% at N >= 12, but it is not separable from the noise at any single N. I therefore claim the exact launch removal and the per-launch kernel saving above, not a specific end-to-end gain. AgentX replay and GSM8K were not run (the epilogue is bit-identical to quantizing the bf16 output in the unit tests). ## Limitations gfx950 FlyDSL decode only; decode-only batches; K = 2048 per rank assumes 16 query heads per KV head with TP4 (generalizes to any heads x 128 since each block is within one head). commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Stop DeepGEMM's MLOPart helper once MegaMoE caches its SM map
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepGEMM MegaMoE leaves an MPS helper process tree alive in every worker for the whole serving lifetime. This makes MegaMoE workers impossible to checkpoint with CUDA checkpoint (as used by [NVIDIA Snapshot](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/snapshot)). This PR stops the helper as soon as DeepGEMM has cached what MegaMoE needs from it. Context: ai-dynamo/snapshot#859.

## Claims

- After startup, a `deep_gemm_mega_moe` worker no longer keeps the DeepGEMM MLOPart helper, MPS control daemon and MPS server alive (8 + 8 + 8 processes on DEP8 → 0).
- MegaMoE kernels read the same cached SM locality-domain map as before, so serving behavior is unchanged: GSM8K and throughput are within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (rev `2cba9e42`), 8×B200, driver 615.71.09, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0`, DEP8 with `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` (the B200 `single_node_dep` recipe flags). "Patched" is the same image with this one-file change mounted over `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`. `get_symm_buffer()` is identical on v0.33.0 and main apart from this change. The two variants were run alternately on the same node.

| Run (in order) | MPS helper trees after startup | GSM8K 5-shot (1319) | Output tok/s, 3 runs | Mean TPOT ms, 3 runs |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| stock | 8 | 90.30% | 5727 / 5944 / 5974 | 9.90 / 9.82 / 9.84 |
| patched | 0 | 90.22% | 5824 / 6057 / 6110 | 9.71 / 9.66 / 9.65 |
| stock | 8 | 90.22% | 5874 / 6443 / 6491 | 9.44 / 9.09 / 9.07 |
| patched | 0 | 90.90% | 6206 / 6469 / 6362 | 9.14 / 9.10 / 9.11 |

Throughput drifts upward across the sequence for both variants. Stock and patched alternate in the lead, so there is no regression.

The same A/B on Vera Rubin: 4x VR200 (compute capability 10.7, driver 620.47), DEP4, `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly` at main `a2bcb565`, whose `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` is identical to this PR's base. The patched runs mount this PR's file. Same flags minus the attention and Engram overrides. (`v0.33.0-aarch64` cannot run DSv4.1 on Rubin: its CUDA 13.0 `ptxas` does not know `sm_107a`.)

| Run (in order) | MPS helper trees after startup | GSM8K 5-shot (1319) | Output tok/s, 3 runs | Mean TPOT ms, 3 runs |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| stock | 4 | 90.14% | 7371 / 7579 / 7671 | 7.99 / 7.97 / 7.91 |
| patched | 0 | 91.58% | 7659 / 7561 / 7690 | 7.93 / 8.00 / 7.90 |
| stock | 4 | 90.52% | 7557 / 7616 / 7648 | 8.00 / 7.98 / 7.93 |
| patched | 0 | 90.07% | 7672 / 7656 / 7619 | 7.95 / 7.93 / 7.96 |

MLOPart is available on VR200 too, so the helper tree is present there and this change removes it. Throughput and TPOT are within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision 2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --engram-config '{"embedding_across_dp":true}'

ps -eo pid,ppid,args --forest | grep -c deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py   # helper trees
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 128
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 640 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed {1,2,3}
```
</details>

With this change, together with the cuInterpose fix in ai-dynamo/snapshot#860, a pod running DeepGEMM's locality-domain probe on B200 can be captured by Snapshot. Without it, capture fails with `cuCheckpointProcessLock: CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

CI coverage: none. The path needs an SM100 GPU on which DeepGEMM can start an MLOPart MPS server, which CI does not provide, so validation was done manually as above.

## Details

**Root cause.** On first use, MegaMoE calls DeepGEMM's `get_balanced_sm_locality_domains()`. DeepGEMM then starts `python -I deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py`, which runs `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with an `-mlopart` MPS server. The helper allocates memory on each die, sends it to the worker as a POSIX FD, and the worker uses it to measure SM-to-die latency. DeepGEMM caches the resulting map and keeps the helper tree until `deep_gemm.destroy_localizer()`. vLLM never calls it. The helper is an MPS client, and the CUDA driver refuses to checkpoint-lock MPS clients, so CUDA checkpoint of any MegaMoE worker fails.

**Fix.** Call `destroy_localizer()` right after `get_symm_buffer()` creates a symmetric buffer, as the [DeepGEMM README](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/82ca617e5879d0efb0aba5b91b1c81852588af6f/README.md) shows. `destroy_localizer()` first computes and caches the balanced map (`get_balanced_sm_locality_domains()`), then stops the helper, so every later kernel launch reads the identical cached tensor.
- **No steady-state change.** The map and the kernel arguments are identical, and the call runs once per new buffer key, never in the forward hot path.
- **Hardware independent.** On a GPU where MLOPart is unavailable, DeepGEMM already uses its even map, and the call changes nothing.
- **No per-die memory affected.** vLLM does not place any MegaMoE memory per die (`deep_gemm.localize`), so nothing still needs the helper.
- **Guard for older DeepGEMM.** The `hasattr` guard keeps externally installed DeepGEMM versions working: `destroy_localizer` first appeared in the 26/09/30 release, while MegaMoE exists since 26/04, and older releases have no helper to stop.
- **Small memory change.** The 8 MPS servers each held 60 MiB of GPU memory, which is now freed. That memory is allocated and released after the worker's initial memory snapshot, so the startup free-memory check is unaffected.

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `destroy_localizer`, `MLOPart` and MegaMoE locality domains. #64835 (closed) placed MegaMoE weights per die and did not address the helper's lifetime. `vllm/distributed/localization.py` is the separate opt-in FlashInfer CuTeDSL path using the native CUDA 13.4 API, and is not affected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][RL] Validate sparse weight patches in one pass
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Validating a sparse weight update launches about ten small GPU ops per patch, which makes it the largest part of the pause on models with many tensors. This validates whole batches of patches at once.

## Claims

- On Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 on H20 (18,867 tensors), the pause drops 40-48% over HTTP under load.
- The saving grows with tensor count: validation goes from about 125 µs to about 5 µs per tensor.
- Verdicts match main in every differential test, with one exception: valid int32 indices into tensors of 2^31 elements or more are no longer rejected.
- Direct callers of `load_checkpoint_weight_patches` get this with no change.

## Validation

**Pause, main against this PR.** Time from the start of `/pause` to the return of `/resume`, median (range):

| Elements changed | Sent | main | This PR | Pause vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1% | 0.17 GiB | 5.75 s (5.21-7.36) | 3.06 s (2.72-4.16) | -47% |
| 1% | 1.71 GiB | 7.14 s (5.71-7.97) | 3.73 s (3.18-4.88) | -48% |
| 3% | 5.12 GiB | 8.99 s (7.83-15.12) | 5.35 s (4.64-5.57) | -40% |

Setup: 4×H20 at TP4 with the trainer on a fifth H20, Triton MoE, main `cb59326ae` wheel, torch 2.14.0+cu130. 2 servers per arm, arms alternating, 8 rounds per density, 32 streaming clients. Patches hold real checkpoint values nudged by 0.1%, at evenly spaced sorted positions.

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --moe-backend triton \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_nccl"}'
```

Each round: `POST /pause?mode=keep`, `SparseNCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine.send_weights(patches)`, `POST /resume`, then 12 s of serving before the next round.

This run uses 0.85 because main runs out of memory above 1% on the default config. Without the flag (1 server per arm, 3 rounds): 6.47 to 3.26 s at 0.1%, 7.44 to 4.79 s at 1%.

- **Output:** `/weight_checker` digests of all 1,740 weights and greedy per-token logprobs are identical across servers, with zero client errors.
- **Same engine, arms alternating:** faster in 30 of 30 pairs, with a median saving of 39-46% per density.
- **Requests:** the longest stall a request sees (p50) goes from 5.70 / 7.25 / 9.13 s to 3.16 / 3.63 / 5.58 s.
- **Throughput:** with 12 s of serving between rounds, 2859 / 2541 / 2237 tok/s become 3152 / 2789 / 2584. A shorter pause also means more rounds per minute, so these are not at the same update rate. Without updates, 4140 and 4089 tok/s on main and 4100 and 4098 here, with TPOT p50 of 6.5-6.6 ms on all four. This code is not on the serving path.

<details>
<summary>Validation alone, one GPU</summary>

Median of 5, with the validation's own peak memory.

| Input | Changed | Duplicate check | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sorted | 0.1% | on | 1954 ms (0.03 GiB) | 82 ms (0.14 GiB) |
| Sorted | 1% | on | 2319 ms (0.11 GiB) | 99 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| Sorted | 3% | on | 2534 ms (0.32 GiB) | 100 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| Sorted | 10% | on | 3479 ms (1.05 GiB) | 149 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| Sorted | 1% | off | 964 ms (0.02 GiB) | 99 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| Reversed | 1% | on | 2342 ms (0.11 GiB) | 1817 ms (0.52 GiB) |
| Reversed | 1% | off | 949 ms (0.02 GiB) | 445 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| BF16/FP32 alternating | 1% | on | 2384 ms (0.11 GiB) | 119 ms (0.42 GiB) |
| One 400M-element patch | - | on | 30 ms (11.97 GiB) | 4 ms (1.86 GiB) |

Larger tensor lists at 0.1%, using only the names and shapes of these checkpoints with synthetic BF16/int32 patches. These engines were not run, so this shows how validation scales, not their pause.

| Checkpoint | Tensors | Duplicate check on | Duplicate check off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 18,867 | 2.40 to 0.09 s | 0.97 to 0.09 s |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 96,085 | 12.6 to 0.52 s | 5.54 to 0.49 s |
| GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 | 148,498 | 17.5 to 0.83 s | 8.61 to 0.79 s |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 152,089 | 18.1 to 0.82 s | 9.64 to 1.01 s |

</details>

**Tests**

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py      # 31 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "sparse or patch"  # 1 passed
VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k "sparse or patch"  # 20 passed, 1 skipped
```

- The 28 cases of the new validation table also pass on main's code, so they pin existing behavior rather than the new implementation.
- All 30 hand-written mutants of the new code fail the new tests. Main's existing test catches 1 of the 29 that target the table.
- 120,000 random CPU rounds and 21 faults injected at real scale (NaN, out of range, negative, duplicates, in the first, middle and last patch) get the same verdicts as main's checks.
- CI: only the AMD Model Executor step selects this test file, because the NVIDIA step is commented out. CI can't reproduce the timing, which needs this model on GPUs.

## Details

**Root cause.** Each patch launches a NaN check, two range comparisons, a sort and a neighbor comparison, plus their reductions. Each launch costs CPU time regardless of size, and the GPU waits are negligible, so the cost follows the number of tensors, not the bytes changed.

**The change.** Patches of one device and dtype are concatenated, up to `max_chunk_bytes`, and checked together:

- NaN: one check over all values.
- Indices that strictly increase within each patch cannot repeat, and each patch's first and last index bound its range. One comparison across the batch establishes this.
- If any patch is out of order, that batch falls back to per-patch min and max, and a per-patch sort when duplicates are checked.

Known producers emit sorted indices: the in-tree example, verl's Megatron export and open-rl.

**Tradeoffs**

- Validation uses more temporary memory: about 0.42 GiB per 512 MiB batch of sorted BF16/int32 patches, 0.52 GiB when reversed, and more for a patch larger than a batch (1.86 GiB for 400M elements, where main uses 1.12 GiB without the duplicate check and 11.97 GiB with it). In the E2E runs the update's allocated peak stayed about the same as main's, because staging dominates. With this model on the default config, main and this PR both pass 1% and run out of memory at 1.25% in staging. This PR doesn't address that limit.
- One out-of-order patch sends its whole batch down the slower path. In my tests that was still faster than main.
- `max_chunk_bytes` now also bounds validation batches, so a very small value slows validation. Known callers use the default.
- A batch reads the GPU twice with `.item()`, where main read once per device. Measured on one GPU, that is 2-22 reads and 0.1-1.3 ms in total, at most 2% of validation. This runs in the weight update RPC while serving is paused, never during inference or inside a CUDA graph.

**Fix in passing.** Main compares int32 indices with a Python int that overflows int32, so it rejects valid indices into tensors of 2^31 elements or more. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has four such tensors. A one-off CPU check with a valid index into a 2^31-element BF16 tensor raises `ValueError` on main and applies here. A test pins this through the validation helper, since the public path would allocate the whole tensor (4 GiB in that check).

**Limits.** One model, TP4, H20 and Triton MoE. Index positions are synthetic, so real training may change the numbers.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `load_checkpoint_weight_patches` and for sparse patch validation, and none changes validation. One open PR edits this file to keep tied embedding patches valid across chunks, in a different function.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DeepGEMM] Match relax warmup M values to the vendored SM100 heuristic
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a dense FP8 runtime-JIT gap in the default `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=relax` mode on SM100. Serving-time token counts can select configurations that startup warmup never probed, triggering nvcc compilation of `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` kernels on the serving critical path. GPU reproduction measured 1.7 seconds per new cubin for weight shapes used by public Qwen3 and MiniMax models.

Related to [#64824](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64824), which tracks remaining DeepGEMM runtime-JIT gaps but does not list this dense-path cause. The duplicate-work check on 2026-11-06 found no open PR touching `_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values`.

Authored with AI assistance.

## Claims

- Expands relax warmup's candidate `block_m` values to match the vendored SM100 dense heuristic; CPU checks cover all 16 candidate multiples, including `block_m=224`.
- GPU validation confirms that the expanded probes eliminate runtime compilation at the previously failing serving M values for both reproduced weight shapes, including a non-swap `block_n` gap.
- The gap is shape-dependent: a host-side scan found uncovered configurations for 39 of 512 eligible N values on a 152-SM part (40 of 512 at 148 SMs). Warmup wall time increased from ~36 s to ~37 s for the measured weight shape.

## Validation

Called the real `_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values` on a CPU-only host with `num_sms=148` and `n=7168`:

| Check | main | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Missing candidate `block_m` multiples | 9 | 0 |
| Probe count at `max_tokens=8192` | 288 | 1060 |

The missing values on main are `[80, 96, 112, 144, 160, 176, 208, 224, 240]`.

An exact host-side port of the vendored SM100 `get_layout_candidates` + `compare` heuristic and vLLM's warmup generator scanned serving M in [1, 8192] across all 512 eligible weight N values (multiples of 128). Real DeepGEMM config selection via `DG_PRINT_CONFIGS=1` matched every sampled point. The scan found these model-level gaps in existing relax warmup:

| Public model(s) | `o_proj` weight (N, K) | Uncovered serving M | Selected configuration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8; Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 | (2048, 4096) | 257–288 | Swap-AB; `block_m=32`, `block_n=128`, cluster (1,2) |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2 | (3072, 6144) | 385–400 on SM100 with 152 SMs | Non-swap; `block_m=128`, `block_n=96`, cluster (2,1) |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2 | (3072, 6144) | 1729–1760 on SM100 with 148 SMs | Non-swap; `block_n=160` |

The Qwen M range overlaps default CUDA-graph capture sizes (multiples of 8 up to 512), so ordinary decode batches can hit it. Negative controls—DeepSeek-V3.x/R1, Kimi-K2, Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, and Qwen3-32B-FP8—had no uncovered serving M in the scan.

GPU reproduction on a GB300 node used dummy FP8 block-quantized weights, with no model download: ran the real `_deepgemm_fp8_gemm_nt_warmup` in relax mode with `max_tokens=8192`, then called `fp8_gemm_nt` at serving M values.

| Weight (N, K) | Existing relax warmup: serving results |
|---|---|
| (2048, 4096) | M=256 cached; M=264 compiled a new cubin (1.7 s); M=272/288 reused it |
| (3072, 6144) | M=384 cached; M=385 compiled a new cubin (1.7 s); M=392/400/401 cached |

Repeating both experiments with `block_ms = list(range(16, 257, 16))` served all previously failing M values from the warmup cache. Measured warmup wall time went from ~36 s to ~37 s for the tested weight shape. These runs validate the reproduced gaps; they do not establish exhaustive GPU coverage of every shape.

Repository pre-commit hooks pass, including ruff and mypy. No unit test was added: a CPU test of the candidate list would mirror the constant without detecting drift in the vendored heuristic. The GPU cache check exercises the actual failure mode and aligns with #64824's `jit_monitor` sub-item.

## Details

`_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values` in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/deep_gemm_warmup.py` hardcodes `block_ms = [64, 128, 256]`, reflecting a 2025-era [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM) heuristic.

The vendored [vllm-project/DeepGEMM](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM) heuristic in `csrc/jit_kernels/heuristics/sm100.hpp` now enumerates `block_m` in steps of 16 through 256 on the swap-AB path. The non-swap candidates `{32, 64, 128}` are a subset. Missing warmup M probes can leave configurations uncovered even when their `block_m` is already in the old list: the MiniMax reproduction is a `block_n` effect.

The fix changes one functional line to `block_ms = list(range(16, 257, 16))` and adds a docstring noting the requirement to stay synchronized with the vendored heuristic. This increases startup probes, with the measured timing above. `full` mode remains the exhaustive, much slower option.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][DSpark] Fuse the Markov bias and block combine into Gumbel sampling
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Speeds up DSpark's Markov sampling loop without changing its output: the Gumbel kernel adds the Markov bias itself, and one kernel replaces the `argmax` + `gather` after it. Split out of #63232.

## Claims

- **Device time:** the sampling part of one Markov step takes 42-50% less time (15.4 -> 7.8 us at 1 row, 91.2 -> 52.9 us at 64 rows; lower is better; 200k vocab, GB300).
- **Kernels:** 9 -> 7 per Markov step, counting the Markov embedding and the bias GEMM.
- **Output:** draft ids and cached draft logits are the same as adding the bias first, so verification stays lossless.

## Validation

**Device time for one Markov step**, in microseconds, lower is better. Timed: the per-step index tensors, the Gumbel kernel, the combine and the copy into `draft_tokens`, plus the bias add where there is one. The Markov embedding and bias GEMM are the same in every arm and are left out.

| rows | `main` | combine kernel only | this PR (combine + fused bias) | saved vs `main` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15.4 | 10.2 | 7.8 | 7.6 us (49.6%) |
| 8 | 26.2 | 21.4 | 15.1 | 11.0 us (42.2%) |
| 64 | 91.2 | 86.8 | 52.9 | 38.3 us (42.0%) |

GB300, BF16 logits and bias, vocab 200,000, temperature 0.8, draft logits cached. CUPTI device time, CUDA graph, cold L2. Each figure is the median of 6 rounds of 50 iterations, with the arm order alternating between rounds; the rounds of an arm stayed within 0.4 us of each other. Every arm first had to match `main`'s tokens and cached logits. The combine kernel saves 4-5 us at every row count; the fused bias saves more as rows grow, because it removes a full-vocab BF16 add per row.

**Same output as `main`,** real engine: Qwen3-4B-FP8 + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`, 7 tokens, probabilistic drafting, 1 GPU, one boot on each tree, autotune off, 32 prompts of 64 tokens.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| greedy token ids | reference | identical on 32 / 32 prompts |
| seeded token ids (temperature 1.0) | reference | identical on 32 / 32 prompts |
| drafts / draft tokens / accepted tokens | 1665 / 11655 / 2470 | 1665 / 11655 / 2470 |
| Python-level draft samples that took the fused path | 0 / 329 | 329 / 329 |

329 is below the draft count because later steps replay from CUDA graphs.

**Tests** on GB300:

```bash
pytest v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py \
  v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  watermarking/test_watermarking.py models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_fused_markov.py
```

392 passed, 0 failed.

`v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py -k dspark` (TP2, batch-sharded vs replicated) also passes, with NUMA wrapping skipped locally: on this host, `main` itself can fail at startup with `Executable was changed during NUMA binding context`, in code this PR does not touch.

New tests:

- `test_markov_chain_matches_adding_bias_first` runs `_sample_markov_chain` on 1024 rows and compares draft ids and cached logits against adding the bias first. It covers the fused path in BF16, FP16 and FP32, and every fallback that needs the sum. It also asserts which path was taken. The row count matters: without rounding the sum in the kernel, the BF16 and FP16 cases fail at 1024 rows but pass at 9, because only near-tied draws flip.
- `test_gumbel_combine_preserves_first_nan_and_maximum` checks the combine kernel against `torch.argmax` + `gather`, including ties, NaN and the masked tail.

Each test was confirmed to fail on the matching mutation: dropping the bias, not rounding the sum, caching the unbiased logits, removing the dtype fallback, picking the last maximum.

Not covered: no end-to-end throughput benchmark, since the kernels above are the whole change. No accuracy eval, since output is unchanged.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:**
  - #63886 (merged) added batch-sharded sequential sampling. This PR builds on the `_sample_markov_chain` it introduced, so it covers both the replicated and the sharded loop.
  - #64442 (merged) and #61869 fuse the loop for DeepSeek-V4.1, and #64031 for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, through a model's own kernels. #62958 is an opt-in int8 Markov walk in a C++ op, and #61824 is greedy-only.
  - This PR keeps the generic Gumbel loop and its draws, so it works with probabilistic drafting and any DSpark draft model that has no fused loop of its own.
- **When the bias is fused:** `_sample_logits` adds the bias up front when it needs the sum: greedy drafting, a reduced draft vocab, watermarking, the acceptance estimator, or logits and bias of different dtypes. `_sample_markov_chain` does the same for Muse Spark's output logit transform. These paths behave as they do on `main`.
- **Rounding:** `logits + bias` rounds in the logits dtype, so the kernel rounds the FP32 sum back to that dtype before adding noise. FP32 holds BF16 and FP16 sums without double-rounding error.
- **Shared code touched:** `gumbel_sample` is also the target sampler, so every caller now uses the combine kernel. It keeps `torch.argmax`'s tie and NaN behavior. The bias path is opt-in and compiles out for other callers.
- **Size:** about 90 non-test lines.
- **Removed from this PR:** the wider DFlash padding, `is_padding` in the positions kernel, the Triton top-k/top-p fix, the temperature-1.0 skip, and the step-major index tensors.

Credits: qizixi (Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel), plus Dao Le, Taoyu Zhu, Zhewen Li, Zijing Liu and xiaozhoupy, whose DSpark work this comes from, as co-authors in the commit. AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes onto `main`, and to write the tests, benchmarks and this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4] Process 4 heads per program in fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant
[Perf][MiniMax-M3] Warm up DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE kernels before serving
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`deep_gemm_warmup` only recognizes DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MoE layers, so MiniMax M3 `nvfp4_mega_moe` kernels JIT on whichever forward reaches them first. This adds `MiniMaxM3MoE` to the MegaMoE warmup and makes the NVFP4 warmup reach both launch variants of a BLOCK_M.

Follows #60468 (DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup) and #64659 (M3 sequence parallel + MegaMoE).

## Claims

- With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, M3 `nvfp4_mega_moe` kernels are compiled in `deep_gemm_warmup`, before autotune and graph capture. Today nothing warms them there: only the token counts reached by dummy runs and capture are compiled, and any other kernel compiles on the first request that needs it.
- The NVFP4 warmup launches the smallest and the largest M of each BLOCK_M, because `decode_shaped` flips inside one BLOCK_M. Keeping only the largest M would miss kernels.
- MX kernels (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3) get the same M values as before.
- No latency or startup-time improvement is claimed or measured. Warmup only, so model output is unaffected.

Example from a Python replica of the DeepGEMM heuristics, using the `MiniMaxM3TextConfig` defaults (128 experts, top-4) at EP4 with 8192 batched tokens (per-rank M up to 2048):

| BLOCK_M | `decode_shaped` | Per-rank M |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | yes | 1-80 |
| 32 | yes | 81-192 |
| 64 | yes | 193-451 |
| 128 | yes | 452-937 |
| 192 | yes | 938-1429 |
| 240 | yes | 1430-1800 |
| 128 | no | 1801-1923 |
| 192 | no | 1924-2048 |

That is 8 kernels across 6 BLOCK_M values. The existing "largest M per BLOCK_M" dedupe would warm 6 and miss the decode-shaped 128 and 192 rows.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/deep_gemm_warmup.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| This change | 10 passed |
| New tests against the base `deep_gemm_warmup.py` | 2 failed, 8 passed: `test_mega_moe_predicate_matches_only_native_mega_moe_layers`, `test_mega_moe_m_values_cover_nvfp4_launch_variants[NVFP4]` |
| pre-commit, including mypy | passed |

The tests ran on an existing build of main at f8b116409c (DeepGEMM a7a9277) with these three files overlaid. `nvfp4_mega_moe.hpp` is identical at a7a9277 and at the current pin, 82ca617.

**Not run:** the unit tests use stand-ins, so the new warmup path has never launched a real `nvfp4_mega_moe` kernel. There was no multi-rank run, no engine startup and no model eval. This is the main thing to check before merging, because a failure here would break startup for M3 MegaMoE deployments rather than just leave a kernel cold. The warmup feeds all-zero hidden states, so every token routes to the same experts, as it already does for DeepSeek-V4; that path is unverified for NVFP4.

## Details

**Duplicate check.** No open PR adds M3 to this warmup. #60995 adds draft models to `deep_gemm_warmup`, so draft coverage is left to it. #64125 moves model warmup registration but doesn't touch `deep_gemm_warmup.py`.

**Both ends of a BLOCK_M.** DeepGEMM doesn't expose `decode_shaped`, and copying the formula here would drift from its heuristics. For a fixed BLOCK_M, `decode_shaped` can only go from true to false as M grows, so the two ends reach both kernels without knowing the threshold. `batched_sf_pulls` either follows `decode_shaped` or stays on, and `compact_dispatch` doesn't depend on M.

**Smaller changes.**
- `MiniMaxM3MoE`'s `input_is_sequence_sharded` is now `use_sequence_parallel`, the name the warmup reads on DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3.
- The warmup key tolerates a gate without `e_score_correction_bias`, since M3 keeps the bias on the MoE.
- The DeepSeek-V4 import moved into the mega-gate branch, so M3 doesn't load that model module.

The existing `fp8_fp4` helper names now also cover NVFP4. I left them to keep the diff small.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] SimpleCPUOffload: one host buffer per rank, opt-in HugeTLB pages
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Functionality**
- `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` allocates each rank's CPU KV caches as views into one host mapping sized to the resolved KV blocks, rounded up to the selected page size. `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` remains the cache budget. Registration is split into chunks of at most 256 GiB, the limit HiSparse already uses, without bisecting a KV block or backing page.
- The new `cpu_hugepage_block_size` key (`"1GB"` or `"2MB"`) backs that mapping with explicit HugeTLB pages; without it, ordinary pages are used.
- The mapping inherits the worker's NUMA memory policy, including vLLM's NUMA binding options or an external launcher policy.
- A HugeTLB pool or container hugetlb limit that's too small fails at startup with an error naming the shortfall, never falling back to 4 KiB pages.
- The mapping is excluded from `fork()` (`MADV_DONTFORK`), so child processes can't make pinned pages copy-on-write.

```json
{"kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both",
 "kv_connector_extra_config": {"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 137438953472,
                               "cpu_hugepage_block_size": "1GB"}}
```

**Performance evidence from the earlier revision**
- In `vllm serve` (TP=2, 64 GiB per rank, ordinary pages), engine init takes 19.0 s vs 20.2 s before.
- With 1 GiB pages, pinning 128 GiB takes 0.19 s instead of 2.5 s on ordinary pages.
- GPU↔CPU copy bandwidth is unchanged at about 42 GB/s.

**Known limitations**
- Registration uses bounded chunks to avoid oversized CUDA registrations (#51081). `pin_tensor`, `unpin_tensor`, and the registration boundary calculation live in `vllm/utils/host_memory.py`, shared by HiSparse and CPU/disk offload as applicable.
- Each rank needs `ceil(resolved cache bytes / page size)` HugeTLB pages, reserved on the host and, on Kubernetes, requested as `hugepages-<size>`.
- Up-front population needs Linux 5.14+ for HugeTLB pages; ordinary pages fall back to first touch on older kernels.

Related: #45693 (same key name for `OffloadingConnector`), #58852, #59430, #51081.

## Validation

The AMD measurements below describe the earlier revision. Current CUDA validation is recorded separately below. NUMA placement now follows the worker policy.

MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, Linux 6.8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-92044241a0` with this PR's three changed files overlaid; the image's copies were byte-identical to this PR's base.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_host_buffer.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py` | 32 passed |
| 8 ranks × 38 GiB (1 GiB pages), random store/load with byte-level checks, 120 s | 0 mismatches; every rank's pages on its GPU's NUMA node |
| More 1 GiB pages than the host has (330 on 320) | Fails at `mmap` with a clear error |
| 150 GiB soak, 10 min, 6,724 concurrent `fork()`s | 0 mismatches |
| `vllm serve` (TP=2, 32 GiB of 1 GiB pages per rank): `SIGKILL` a worker, `SIGKILL` the engine core, `SIGTERM`, then restart; plus `SIGKILL`/`SIGSEGV`/exception at buffer level, including mid-populate, mid-pin, and with forked children still alive | Requests served; the HugeTLB pool and GPU memory return to baseline within 5 s each time, and the restarted engine serves |

The 8-rank, soak and pool rows ran on the previous revision, which populated pages with 16 threads; this revision populates with one `madvise` call and was re-checked with the unit tests and the `vllm serve` crash/restart row.

The earlier AMD validation did not include CUDA or an offload-on/off output comparison. The subsequent CUDA runs below include a small-model output smoke comparison; a full model-accuracy evaluation remains outstanding. AMD CI already runs `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload`; the HugeTLB tests skip on hosts without a pool.

### Review fixes (`76365e976b`, `de6a707b43`)

These AI-assisted fixes allocate only the resolved cache bytes, inherit NUMA policy, and preserve one registration per matching unregister. Shared helpers moved to `vllm/utils/host_memory.py`; their function ASTs are unchanged by the move. The independent HIP SDMA optimization is handled by #65559.

- An isolated reproduction showed that the original chunked `pin_tensor` left one registered range after HiSparse teardown for a tensor larger than 1 GiB. `pin_tensor` now registers exactly one range again.
- Pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_hisparse_registration_chunks_end_between_host_blocks`: collection blocked by missing FlashAttention CUDA extensions. The environment was not modified.
- Subsequent CUDA integration and output smoke results are recorded below. No before/after performance benchmark was run.


### CUDA validation and alignment fix (`26bcba935b`, 2026-11-05)

Validated on an exclusive Slurm node with 4 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs, driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0 / PyTorch 2.14.0, and Linux 6.17 with 64 KiB OS pages. The isolated environment used this PR's Python source and native/generated dependencies from `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5`.

The first large HugeTLB run exposed a real bug: under NUMA binding, a registration ending inside a 2 MiB backing page returned `cudaErrorInvalidValue`. For example, registering `1 GiB - 64 KiB` failed while a whole `1 GiB` succeeded on the same mapping. The shared boundary helper now receives the actual backing-page size; HiSparse keeps its OS-page default. The previously failing four-rank scenario passed after this correction.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Targeted host-buffer, worker, mixed-layout, ordering, boundary and NUMA integration tests | 16 passed; 1 skipped because this kernel has no 1 GiB HugeTLB support |
| Four concurrent HugeTLB ranks, 38/38/12/12 GiB, 120 s | 21,792 byte-exact round trips, zero mismatches; all pages on the configured NUMA nodes |
| 150 GiB ordinary-page soak, 600 s, concurrent forks | 18,490 round trips and 36,980 forks, zero mismatches |
| Qwen3-0.6B NUMA integration | Restored 16 CPU KV blocks; generated token IDs matched the cold result |
| Qwen3-0.6B serving, TP=2, 32 GiB HugeTLB per rank | Three greedy prompts matched offload-disabled outputs; restart served successfully |
| Worker SIGKILL / engine SIGKILL / server SIGTERM | HugeTLB pool and GPU memory returned to baseline in 4.10 / 3.38 / 0.58 s |
| 32 GiB buffer: SIGKILL during population, SIGKILL after partial registration, SIGSEGV, exception | All resources recovered in under 1 s; core dumps disabled |
| Final cleanup | HugeTLB configuration restored to zero pages, all GPUs at zero allocated MiB, container removed, Slurm allocation released |

The ordinary-page soak started before the HugeTLB alignment correction; its OS-page arithmetic is unchanged, and ordinary-page focused tests passed again afterward. The CUDA run uses four ranks rather than the earlier eight-rank AMD setup. NUMA node 1 could reserve only about 25.9 GiB of 2 MiB pages, so its two ranks used 12 GiB each. This validates 2 MiB HugeTLB on GB200, not 1 GiB pages or all CUDA platforms. The output check is a three-prompt serving smoke test, not a full accuracy evaluation. No speedup is claimed from these runs.

This commit also extended the existing boundary test to HugeTLB page sizes. Pre-commit checks, including mypy, passed.

### Simplification (`2a6867aa5c`)

- The registration chunk limit is now the shared `HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_BYTES` (256 GiB) instead of 1 GiB. With a 1 GiB limit and 1 GiB pages, every boundary had to be a 1 GiB multiple that is also a block boundary, so any block size that does not divide 1 GiB (for example MLA: 576 × 2 × 64 = 73728 B) failed at startup. With the larger limit, a boundary exists at lcm(block, page), which is 9 GiB in that example. HiSparse behavior is unchanged.
- `HostBuffer` is now a function, `alloc_host_buffer()`, because `torch.frombuffer` keeps the mapping alive. It reuses the existing `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` helper and its pre-5.14 fallback from `shared_offload_region.py`. `cpu_hugepage_block_size` accepts only the documented `2MB`, `1GB` and `none`.
- The docs section, comments and the populate/pin timing log are shorter.
- Tests check page rounding, HugeTLB pool consumption, fail-closed allocation and a GPU→CPU→GPU round trip on ordinary and HugeTLB pages. They no longer read smaps flags, kernel zeroing or private attributes. The single-fix pin/unpin test and the unrelated `served_model_name` change to the integration test were removed.
- Validation: pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passed. `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_host_buffer.py`: 7 passed, 2 skipped (no free hugepages on the host). `test_worker.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py` could not be collected locally because the FlashAttention CUDA extensions are missing; they rely on CI. The GB200 runs above predate this commit.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this preset. #65400 and #63547 also edit this file, but I found no hunk touching this preset.

## Claims

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-4fab5a07475822c6eaa971dceb2e2220d0446808@sha256:6f126f27…` (vLLM main of 2026-11-05) replaces the day-zero `minimax-m31-flash` image, so the MiniMax-M3.1 ROCm kernels merged since (#64448, #63637, #65087, #65432, #65478, #65481, #65530, #65386, #65267) are in the recipe's image.
- Switches that default off are now set at every point: `VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK=1`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0` (alongside the existing `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO_DRAFTER=1`).
- Concurrency 16 and 32 run breakable CUDA graphs (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, multiple-of-8 capture list); dual-batch overlap is removed from the 16-64 points.
- Runbook table and notes refreshed from the new run. InferenceX run 42224368840 at `ce4079c48`: p90 interactivity +8-22% at concurrency 1-8, +22% at 16, +16% at 32, +26% at 64 against the previous revision's run 41003224750; total tokens/s per GPU +2-20% at every point; GSM8K strict 0.961 / 0.963 / 0.960 at concurrency 8 / 32 / 64.

## Validation

Validated with the recipes repository's own checks (the `Recipes` PR check runs the first one):

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes   # valid against the renderer
```

and by rendering all seven points with the renderer's `renderCommand` (the function that builds the site's commands) for the old and new file. The delta per point is exactly what InferenceX #4866 changed and nothing else: new image at every point; `+VLLM_ROCM_PARALLEL_INDEX_TOPK`, `+VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`, `+VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` at every point; at concurrency 16 and 32 additionally `+VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH`, `+--compilation-config` and `-` the three DBO flags; at 64 `-` the DBO flags. Concurrency 1-8 render unchanged otherwise.

| Concurrency | p50 / p90 interactivity (tokens/s/user) | total tokens/s per GPU | previous revision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 604.4 / 590.1 | 7,617 | 551.0 / 515.7, 6,766 |
| 2 | 608.4 / 446.2 | 7,588 | 548.9 / 410.4, 6,918 |
| 4 | 610.2 / 428.3 | 9,698 | 546.3 / 395.6, 9,494 |
| 8 | 450.2 / 292.2 | 16,104 | 407.4 / 240.0, 15,411 |
| 16 | 313.5 / 204.6 | 28,686 | 228.6 / 168.3, 27,275 |
| 32 | 220.9 / 133.7 | 58,024 | 172.3 / 115.1, 54,158 |
| 64 | 95.1 / 59.7 | 90,495 | 71.4 / 47.3, 75,434 |

All numbers are single runs; no end-to-end run of this recipe's commands was done outside InferenceX.

## Details

- **Why the validator alone is not enough.** My first version passed validation but rendered concurrency 16 and 32 without `--compilation-config`: a preset's `json_args` can only edit a flag, and `--compilation-config` belongs to the `mono_decode` feature, so it was silently dropped where mono is not selected. It is now a plain argument.
- **Concurrency 16 first attempt was an outlier** (ITL p50 5.64 ms, slower than concurrency 32, GPU power 9% down, on one node); the rerun on another node gave the figures above (ITL p50 3.19 ms). The cause was not isolated, so treat 16 as one good run. This is stated in the runbook.
- **DBO and the graphs changed together.** DBO was on at 16-64 before; the gain at those points is the combined effect, not DBO alone. Also stated in the runbook.

- **Source pin.** `source.revision` is the InferenceX head `ce4079c48`; if #4866 changes before it merges, the revision, table and notes need a refresh. Concurrency 64 uses the host KV tier and was not rerun (the previous revision's first attempt hung at the first host-tier load).

commits.pr_title: [CPU][Perf] Speed up GDN speculative-decode recurrent update
commits.pr_body:
**Purpose:** Speed up `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`, which runs in every GDN layer during speculative-decode verify on CPU (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.6 with DFlash/MTP).
- Work is split over (sequence, value head, 64-column block) instead of (sequence, value head). At batch 1, Qwen3.6 now has 64 work items instead of 32.
- Each item loads its fp32 state block once and keeps it in cache across all draft tokens. The old kernel re-read the previous slot twice per token.
- The per-token intermediate states, which are only read again on a later step, are written with streaming stores (AVX-512, aligned addresses). This avoids the read-for-ownership on every store.

**Test plan:**
- New `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`: fp32/bf16/fp16 state; uneven, empty and 0-accepted rows; value dim not a multiple of the vector width. All existing GDN CPU tests pass.
- New `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_gdn_spec.py`: cold-state, 30 layers.

**Results (GCP c4-standard-48, 23 threads):**
- Kernel, 30 layers, 8 tokens: fp32 state 9.01 → 4.91 ms (−45%); bf16 state 4.90 → 2.61 ms (−47%).
- End-to-end, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash2 (7 speculative tokens), HumanEval, concurrency 1: median ITL 127.85 → 120.08 ms (−6.1%), mean TPOT 23.23 → 22.07 ms (−5.0%), output throughput 38.17 → 39.92 tok/s (+4.6%). Acceptance length 5.58 vs 5.53.

**Kernel, batch scaling (fp32 state, 8 tokens per request, 30 layers):**

 | batch | before | after |
 |---|---|---|
 | 1 | 8.97 ms | 5.45 ms (−39%) |
 | 4 | 28.60 ms | 20.77 ms (−27%) |
 | 16 | 110.86 ms | 82.89 ms (−25%) |

 **Accuracy:** gsm8k (5-shot, limit 200) through the full DFlash2 + Qwen3.6-35B-A3B server: 0.290 after vs 0.295 before (±0.032 standard error). Outputs are not bit-identical: the summation order changed, and with bf16/fp16 state the running state stays fp32 between draft tokens within a step.

 **Tests:**
 - `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py`: 224 passed, including the new spec-kernel test with an unaligned state cache.
 - `pytest tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py -k mtp`: Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN) with MTP, 1 passed.

Assisted by GHCP.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stop declaring the MXFP4 MoE intermediate padding to AITER
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with

```
AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan)
```

(e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on
vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against.

AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch
buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them
where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is
NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a
non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have
run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure.
Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568

## This change

Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant
there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path.

Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and
stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call:

| step | padded region | where |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` |
| checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for it and its docstring calls out "padding ... on the shard (intermediate) dimension (e.g. for MXFP4 GEMM)" | `RoutedExperts._narrow_expert_data_for_padding`, used by `_load_w13` / `_load_w2` right before `expert_data.copy_()` |
| weight shuffle | pure `view` + `permute` (asserts `N % 16 == 0`, `K % 32 == 0`, no re-padding), so zeros stay zeros | `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight` |
| scale shuffle | re-pads the scale to 256 rows / 8 cols, but fills the pad with `0x7F` (E8M0 = 1.0) before copying, so it is never garbage | `aiter.utility.fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle` |

So for the padded columns the kernel computes

- stage 1: `x @ 0 = 0` (gate and up are both zero there, and the bias is zero,
  so the activation output is exactly `silu(0) * 0 = 0`)
- stage 2: `0 @ 0 = 0`

Exact zeros also mean the padded columns cannot disturb the stage-2 activation
quantization: `amax` over an MX group is unaffected by zeros, whether or not a
group straddles real and padded columns.

Two things are deliberately left alone:

- **`hidden_pad`** — the activation columns it covers are not guaranteed to be
  zero, so dropping it would not be equivalent.
- **SITU** (`activation == MoEActivation.SITU`, the a16w4 FlyDSL port used by
  Kimi K3) — that kernel consumes the pad. The surrounding code already skips
  the rounding for it ("SITU's A16W4 FlyDSL kernel pads per gate/up half; pass
  through unrounded"), and on that path AITER keys its own scratch
  initialization on the value: `_alloc = torch.zeros if inter_dim_pad > 0 else
  torch.empty` in `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`. Zeroing the declaration
  there would *remove* an initialization that is currently happening, which is
  the opposite of what this PR is for.

This is a workaround and should be reverted once the AITER fix is merged and
pinned. The surrounding code already carries a similar TODO about AITER padding
behaviour.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, stock AITER 0.1.25 — i.e. **without** the
AITER-side fix — running `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` unmodified,
each run covering TP2 and TP4:

| build | runs | cells | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly this patch | 4 | 8 | **all passed** |
| same logic, earlier iterations of the comment/wording | 10 | 20 | **all passed** |

14 runs, 28 cells, no NaN. Before the change the same test failed intermittently
— locally about 2 runs in 6 — so 14 clean runs is about 0.3% likely if the
change did nothing.

Overhead: none measurable. Timing the same shape with and without the
declaration (median over 6 rounds, per `fused_moe_2stages` call):

| M | declared | not declared |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.139 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 4 | 0.156 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 1439 | 0.534 ms | 0.536 ms |
| 16384 | 2.010 ms | 2.010 ms |

All within run-to-run noise (~4%).

## Scope and limits

- Validated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 (`model_dim=5120`, per-rank
  intermediate 576 padded to 640, E=384, topk=6). Other MXFP4 models on this
  path (e.g. gpt-oss with INTERLEAVE) are covered by the same zero-fill
  argument but were not run here, so reviewers may prefer a narrower gate.
- The zero-fill chain above is established from the code, with the citations in
  the table. It is not confirmed by a run against a real MXFP4 checkpoint that
  actually has padding: the test that exercises this path uses a random-weight
  loader which also zero-fills the padding, and every MXFP4 checkpoint we have
  locally has `moe_intermediate_size = 2048`, which is already aligned per rank
  (pad = 0). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2304) is the one that pads, and the local copy
  of it is FP8 rather than MXFP4.
- Models whose per-rank intermediate size is already 128-aligned get
  `intermediate_pad == 0` and are unaffected either way.
- The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` opt-in is a sub-case of
  `use_mxfp4_w4a16`, so it is covered by this change as well. The same
  zero-fill argument applies to it, but it runs different kernels and was not
  exercised here.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][DP] Hash the parallel config before engine init for DP validation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `data_parallel_size > 1`, a `NixlConnector` and `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`, every engine fails the DP configuration check at READY since #62330. The READY message now carries the hash of the parallel config the engine was started with, which is the config the front-end compares it against (#26218).

## Claims

- Fixes the startup failure `Configuration mismatch detected for engine N ... Worker hash: ..., Expected hash: ...` for DP > 1 deployments that rely on the automatic `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` resolve (NIXL + DCP). The set of compared fields is unchanged, only the moment of hashing moves.
- One file, +12/-4, no new configuration and no user-visible behaviour change.

## Validation

- Root cause reproduced on a live deployment at `44965a1097` (2026-11-03): an MLA MoE model (GLM-5.3 shape), one engine per node, `--data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 1 --data-parallel-rank N --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", ...}'`. Every rank exits at READY with the mismatch, right after logging `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size is automatically adjusted from 1 to block_size 64`. Recomputing the front-end's `ParallelConfig.compute_hash()` factors inside the running API server reproduces the "Expected hash"; changing the single factor `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` from 1 to 64 reproduces the "Worker hash" exactly.
- Workaround confirmed on the same deployment: `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64` (which turns the auto-resolve off) brings all four ranks to READY.
- The patch passes `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` with the repository configuration. The hash is computed from the same `ParallelConfig` fields as before, after `startup_handshake` has applied the coordinator's updates, so a real mismatch (for example a different `--enable-expert-parallel` on one rank) is still detected.

## Details

Root cause. #26218 added `parallel_config_hash` to the READY message, computed in `EngineCoreProc._perform_handshake` after the generator resumes, that is after `EngineCore.__init__` has run. #62330 moved `VllmConfig.adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` into `_initialize_kv_caches`, before profiling, so with NIXL + DCP and no explicit size the engine's `parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` becomes the block size before the hash is taken. `wait_for_engine_startup` compares that hash with the front-end's `ParallelConfig`, which still holds the default, and `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is not in `compute_hash`'s `ignored_factors`.

Change. `_perform_handshake` computes `parallel_config.compute_hash()` right after `startup_handshake` returns and before the `yield`, and sends the stored value in the READY message. Handshake-time updates (`data_parallel_size`, the master address and port) are still included; the front-end applies the same updates to its own config, as before.

Alternative considered. Adding `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to `ParallelConfig.compute_hash`'s `ignored_factors`. That hash also feeds `VllmConfig.compute_hash`, the compile cache key, where the interleave size matters, and the same mismatch would come back with the next setting the engine resolves after startup. Hashing before initialization covers both.

Related. #60671 (open) moves the NIXL + DCP interleave resolve into `VllmConfig` so that both processes hold the resolved value. This change is the minimal fix for the check itself and stands on its own; the two compose.
