commits.pr_title: [Perf] Vectorize silu_and_mul_per_block_quant for large inputs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` launches one 128-thread block per (token, group). Each thread issues one 2-byte load, and the group max is a shared-memory tree reduction. At prefill sizes the kernel runs at ~0.9 TB/s on H200. It is therefore 1.3-2.2x *slower* than the unfused `silu_and_mul` + `per_token_group_quant_fp8` pair it replaces.

This PR adds a vectorized variant (16B loads, warp-shuffle reduction, 8B stores) for large inputs. The existing kernel stays for small inputs, where it has lower latency. Both produce bitwise-identical results.

## Claims

- At >= 16k rows the fused kernel is 2.0-2.45x faster than before, and now 8-53% faster than the unfused pair. At <= 64 rows (decode) it is unchanged. See the table below.
- Paths that use the fused kernel today get faster prefill:
  - the Triton FP8 MoE with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0`;
  - the `SiluMul+BlockQuant` compile fusion, where it matches.
- Prerequisite for #65794, which enables the fused path by default (superseding #64906 and #43399). With the old kernel, that change costs -3.8% prefill on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8.

## Validation

**Kernel:** H200, bf16 in, fp8 out, group 128, CUDA-graph timed, p10 µs.

| 2I | rows | unfused (silu_and_mul + group quant) | fused, main | fused, this PR | vs main |

| 1536 | 8 | 3.88 | 1.88 | **1.91** | 0.98x |
| 1536 | 64 | 4.05 | 2.07 | **2.07** | 1.00x |
| 1536 | 512 | 4.59 | 3.94 | **3.29** | 1.20x |
| 1536 | 4096 | 10.98 | 18.25 | **9.48** | 1.93x |
| 1536 | 16384 | 36.93 | 74.68 | **32.52** | 2.30x |
| 1536 | 65536 | 133.29 | 292.75 | **121.94** | 2.40x |
| 4096 | 8 | 3.97 | 1.98 | **1.97** | 1.01x |
| 4096 | 64 | 4.18 | 2.54 | **2.53** | 1.00x |
| 4096 | 512 | 5.95 | 7.38 | **4.60** | 1.60x |
| 4096 | 4096 | 25.55 | 48.17 | **22.28** | 2.16x |
| 4096 | 16384 | 91.15 | 197.16 | **82.37** | 2.39x |
| 4096 | 65536 | 349.48 | 783.51 | **320.24** | 2.45x |
| 24576 | 8 | 5.73 | 2.32 | **2.31** | 1.00x |
| 24576 | 64 | 6.37 | 5.98 | **3.95** | 1.51x |
| 24576 | 512 | 20.94 | 34.80 | **17.11** | 2.03x |
| 24576 | 4096 | 144.98 | 293.35 | **121.90** | 2.41x |
| 24576 | 16384 | 560.98 | 1166.89 | **478.78** | 2.44x |

**End to end:** `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, H200 TP1, `--moe-backend auto` (Triton), `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0` (the configuration where main already uses the fused kernel). Two runs per arm, interleaved.

| | prefill in tok/s | mixed out tok/s | TPOT c1 | TPOT c8 | TPOT c32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (run 1 / run 2) | 65,752 / 64,061 | 7,630 / 7,781 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.86 / 5.85 | 8.33 / 8.54 |
| this PR (run 1 / run 2) | **67,634 / 69,375** | 7,855 / 7,829 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.89 / 5.87 | 8.45 / 8.24 |

Prefill is +5.6% (mean of two), mixed +1.7%, and decode unchanged. Workloads, all `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`:
- prefill: 4096 in / 1 out, concurrency 64, 256 prompts
- mixed: 1024 / 512, concurrency 128
- decode: 1024 / 256 at concurrency 1/8/32

With the default `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` the Triton MoE path does not use the fused kernel on main, so this PR is a no-op there today.

**Tests:**
- New `test_silu_and_mul_per_block_quant_vec_matches_scalar`: the vectorized path vs the scalar path, forced by a 2-byte-misaligned view of the same input. It asserts bitwise equality over bf16/fp16, fp8/int8, group sizes 64/128, and both scale layouts.
- The existing reference tests already hit the vectorized path through their large shapes (512x5120, 256x14336, and the int32-offset-overflow case).
- `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py`: 347 passed (331 on main, plus the 16 new cases).
- `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_{,manual_}fusion.py`: 126 passed, the same as main.

## Details

**Mapping:** each group is handled by `group_size / 8` lanes (16 for group 128), each owning 8 contiguous elements of gate and up. The max is reduced with `__shfl_xor_sync` over those lanes, and lane 0 writes the scale.

**Dispatch:** the vectorized kernel is used for 16-bit inputs with 16B-aligned input and 8B-aligned output, when `num_tokens * num_groups >= 3072`. The threshold is measured: at <= 2048 groups the one-block-per-group kernel is ~0.4-0.9 µs faster, and above ~3072 groups the vectorized one wins. Misaligned views fall back to the existing kernel.

**Arithmetic:** identical to the existing kernel (`gate * (1 / (1 + exp(-gate))) * up`, `max(amax / qmax, min_scale)`, `x / scale`). The file is not built with `--use_fast_math`.

**Overlaps:**
- #62386 edits the same file (TMA-aligned scale stride). The changes are orthogonal, but whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #43399 (UE8M0 option) also touches this kernel; the vectorized variant takes the same template flags if both land.

**Duplicate check:** no open PR changes this kernel's performance.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Respect padded row strides in top-k routing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56900.

Inductor can produce router logits with padded physical rows, for example shape
`[M, 60]` and stride `(64, 1)`. The native MoE top-k path used
`blockIdx.x * num_experts` to locate each input row, so it read the wrong logits
whenever the physical row stride differed from `num_experts`. This silently
changed expert routing under compilation.

This change:

- propagates `gating_output.stride(0)` to the native top-k launcher;
- uses the existing unfused softmax/sigmoid plus top-k path for padded rows;
- allocates the required workspace for padded power-of-two expert counts;
- keeps packed rows on the existing specialized path; and
- adds regression coverage for softmax and sigmoid with 60/64 and 64/72
  logical/physical row widths.

The input-row offset is `int64_t` because PyTorch tensor strides are 64-bit;
this also avoids 32-bit wraparound in the input address calculation. Open PR
[#53131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53131) independently widens
packed-row pointer arithmetic more broadly, but it does not propagate
`stride(0)` or handle padded rows. The two changes overlap only on the
input-offset width; this PR addresses the separate functional stride bug.

No open PR referencing #56900 or implementing padded-row support for this
kernel was found before submission.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py \
  -k padded_row_stride

EXPECTED_VLLM="$(.venv/bin/python -c 'import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)')"
.venv/bin/python \
  /workspace/fp-atomics-census/probes/diagnostics/moe_compile/moe_compile_reproducer.py \
  --output-dir /workspace/results-56900/patched-e2e \
  --runners v2 \
  --compiles on off \
  --graphs off \
  --expected-vllm "$EXPECTED_VLLM"
```

The same focused cases were also run with a standalone kernel reproducer before
and after rebuilding vLLM from source. The end-to-end command uses the
[issue reproducer](https://github.com/catmcgee/fp-atomics-census/blob/2137e7b6347c0027fc48e5cd66b1f7d86e5ad2e4/probes/diagnostics/moe_compile/moe_compile_reproducer.py).
Each end-to-end arm ran in a fresh process with separate vLLM, Inductor, and
Triton cache roots.

## Test Result

| Check | Baseline | Patched |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Kernel reproducer | failed as expected; minimum 3/33 matching rows | passed; 33/33 in all four cases |
| Focused padded-stride pytest | not applicable | 4 passed |
| Compiled duplicate-prompt pairs | 0/8 | 8/8 |
| Compiled short-cycle outputs | 9 | 0 |
| Eager duplicate-prompt pairs | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| Eager short-cycle outputs | 0 | 0 |

The end-to-end control used
`Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat` at revision
`ec052fda178e241c7c443468d2fa1db6618996be` with the 16-prompt duplicate
batch from #56900. The compiled and eager arms held the model runner and
selected backends fixed; only compilation mode changed.

Validation environment:

- NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3, compute capability 9.0
- CUDA 13.0 (`nvcc` 13.0.88), driver 580.126.09
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`
- vLLM source commit `0748d3bd57cb5c4303e58c8465e21f069629480d`

Pre-commit passed on both changed files. The validated source files are
unchanged between the tested commit and the current PR base.

## AI assistance

validation planning. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and model
evaluation reported above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return 400 for images rejected by Pillow's bomb check
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` lets Pillow's `DecompressionBombError` escape, so an image above Pillow's pixel limit gets an HTTP 500 from the API server. This converts it to a `ValueError` like the other undecodable-image errors, so the client gets a 400.

Fixes #60303

## Claims

- A 23 KB PNG of 14000x14000 pixels (196M pixels, above the 178,956,970 default of both Pillow's 2x limit and `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`) changes from `500 InternalServerError` to `400 BadRequestError`.
- `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` now raises `ValueError` for these images instead of `PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError`, so `MediaConnector.fetch_image`, `fetch_image_async` and the `video/jpeg` frame path of `VideoMediaIO.load_base64` report them as client errors too.
- No change to which images are accepted or rejected, and no change to the `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` check.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), CPU only, Pillow 12.3.0. It builds the PNG, calls the same `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async` that `chat_utils` uses for an `image_url` part, and puts that behind vLLM's registered exception handlers:

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
from io import BytesIO
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pybase64
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image

from vllm.entrypoints.serve.exception_handling.register import init_exception_handler
from vllm.multimodal.media import ImageMediaIO, MediaConnector

buf = BytesIO()
Image.new("1", (14000, 14000)).save(buf, format="PNG")
data = buf.getvalue()
print("png bytes", len(data), "pixels", 14000 * 14000)

try:
    ImageMediaIO().load_bytes(data)
except BaseException as e:
    print("load_bytes ->", type(e).__module__ + "." + type(e).__name__,
          "| is ValueError:", isinstance(e, ValueError), "|", str(e)[:160])

url = "data:image/png;base64," + pybase64.b64encode(data).decode()

app = FastAPI()
app.state.args = SimpleNamespace(log_error_stack=False)
init_exception_handler(app)


@app.post("/v1/chat/completions")
async def chat():
    await MediaConnector().fetch_image_async(url)


r = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).post("/v1/chat/completions")
print("HTTP", r.status_code, r.json())
```

</details>

Before (`main`):

```text
png bytes 23859 pixels 196000000
load_bytes -> PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError | is ValueError: False | Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.
HTTP 500 {'error': {'message': 'Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.', 'type': 'InternalServerError', 'param': None, 'code': 500}}
```

After (this PR):

```text
png bytes 23859 pixels 196000000
load_bytes -> builtins.ValueError | is ValueError: True | Failed to load image: Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.
HTTP 400 {'error': {'message': 'Failed to load image: Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
```

Regression test `test_image_decompression_bomb_rejected` in `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`. It lowers `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` so a 20x20 PNG trips Pillow's limit, and checks that `load_bytes` raises `ValueError` caused by `Image.DecompressionBombError`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -v
```

- On `main` with only the test added: `1 failed, 13 passed`. The failure is `PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError: Image size (400 pixels) exceeds limit of 100 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.` raised from `open_image` in `load_bytes`.
- With the fix: `14 passed`.

Wider run, `tests/multimodal/media` (CPU only):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media -q
```

- `main`: `3 failed, 162 passed, 4 skipped`.
- This PR: `3 failed, 163 passed, 4 skipped` (the added test).
- The 3 failures are the same on both and unrelated: `test_audio.py::test_audio_media_io_from_video`, `test_load_audio_backend_matches_default[pyav]` and `test_audio_media_io_audio_backend_kwarg` fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'av'` because my environment lacks `vllm[audio]`. The 4 skips are `torchcodec` not being installed.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `test_image_decompression_bomb_rejected` fails with `image.py` reverted to `main` (`PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError: Image size (400 pixels) exceeds limit of 100 pixels`) and passes with the fix.
- The repro above still returns `HTTP 500` on `main`.
- `pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`: 14 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py vllm/multimodal/media/image.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `Image.open` calls Pillow's `_decompression_bomb_check`, which raises `Image.DecompressionBombError` for an image above `2 * Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (178,956,970 pixels by default). That class derives from `Exception`, not `OSError`, so the `except (OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)` in `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` does not catch it. The raw exception propagates through `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async` and `AsyncMultiModalItemTracker.resolve_items`, and `create_error_response` has no mapping for it, so it falls through to `InternalServerError` (500). A `ValueError` takes the `BadRequestError` (400) branch.

The default `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (178,956,970) equals Pillow's 2x threshold, and Pillow's check runs inside `Image.open`, before the `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` check. So with default settings an oversized image is always stopped by Pillow first, and the 400 that `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` is meant to provide (see `docs/usage/security.md`) is only reachable once the variable is lowered. The variable does not change Pillow's limit, so raising it or setting it to `0` leaves the same 500.

The fix adds `Image.DecompressionBombError` to the exception tuple, so the message is reported as `Failed to load image: ...` with the original exception chained. It is the same treatment #38253 gave truncated and corrupt images.

Scope and limits:

- Pillow's own limit stays in force. Images between `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and twice that still only produce Pillow's `DecompressionBombWarning` and load as before.
- Only the exception type seen by callers changes. Nothing is decoded that was not decoded before.

Not a duplicate. I searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs, open and closed, for `DecompressionBombError`, `decompression bomb`, `DecompressionBombWarning`, `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, `ImageMediaIO` and `oversized image 500`, and listed open PRs matching `multimodal/media/image.py`, `decompression bomb image` and `Pillow image error`. Nothing covers this bug. Closest hits:

- #47010 (merged) added `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and the pixel check in `load_bytes`. It does not handle the exception Pillow raises from `Image.open`.
- #38253 (merged) returned 400 for corrupt or truncated images. It covers `OSError` and `UnidentifiedImageError` only.
- #56527 (closed issue) is a 500 from malformed EXIF in `MultiModalHasher.serialize_item`, a different code path.
- #57752 (open, marked "Don't merge", `needs-rebase`) is an experiment that moves media decoding into the multimodal processor. It keeps the same `except (OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)` tuple, so it does not address this and would need the same one-line addition if it lands.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DP] Log cross-engine step statistics ordering at debug level
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Log DP coordinator out-of-order step reports at DEBUG instead of WARNING. Reports from different engines can arrive in a different step order even when each engine reports in order.

## Claims

- Avoid per-report warning output for cross-engine statistics arrival skew at the default log level; retain the diagnostic at DEBUG.
- Preserve all statistics updates, step snapshots, and wave coordination.

## Validation

- Existing run evidence: a saved audit of a 32-rank DP deployment counted 1,751,591 occurrences, totaling 290,881,789 bytes. All reports had the same wave as the global latest report; 1,751,578 lagged by one step and 13 by two steps. This is evidence of logging volume, not a measured throughput improvement.
- `ruff check vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed.
- `ruff format --check vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed.
- `python -m py_compile vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed, using the existing venv.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py docs/usage/troubleshooting.md` — all applicable checks passed, including mypy and Markdown lint.
- Tests and model evaluations were not run. The sole executable change is the diagnostic level; no inference or statistics-processing behavior changes. No new test was added solely to assert log severity. Runtime validation remains pending for this draft.

## Details

The comparison is against one global `(wave, step)` position. For example, engine A's step 101 may arrive before engine B's step 100, causing a warning even if B's previous report was step 99. The warning alone does not establish same-engine message regression or a failed request.

This is a logging-only alternative to #52936, which adds per-engine position tracking and rejects regressing reports. It does not add state or discard reports, and it does not claim to repair cross-engine snapshot consistency. The original snapshot/load-balancing design from #21617 remains intact. Open-PR searches found #52936 but no separate logging-only fix.

The troubleshooting guide documents the diagnostic and how to enable it with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`. The tradeoff is reduced default visibility of this ordering diagnostic, including any anomalous cases that reach the same branch.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and PR (the exact underlying model version was not exposed); `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` assisted with source analysis and checklist review. This is a draft for human review.

commits.pr_title: [Startup] Skip the CUDA graph memory profile when its estimate is disabled
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Cleanup: with `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`, `determine_available_memory()` still runs `profile_cudagraph_memory()` and then ignores the result. Skip the call when the flag is 0. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR; I reviewed every changed line.

Since #56492 (extensible KV cache), MRV2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` returns 0 when the extensible cache is on. The startup saving therefore applies only to fallback configurations (MRV1, elastic EP, `LMCacheMPConnector`, etc.) with the flag at 0.

## Claims

Fallback configurations with the flag at 0 no longer run the throwaway capture pass. On current main the pass costs:

| Fallback configuration | Estimate pass on main | Startup, main → this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2, `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` | 89 s, 90 s | 260.8 s → 171.0 s |
| MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 3 s, 3 s | within run-to-run noise |

Setup: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, one GB300, `--compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 4096}'`, `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`, warm caches, main at c96e5f60bb. The estimate pass is the span from vLLM's `Profiling CUDA graph memory` log line to `Estimated CUDA graph memory` (MRV1), and the first `Graph capturing finished` line (MRV2). The real capture takes the same time with and without this PR (MRV2: 95 s and 96 s). The earlier 95.1 s → 72.5 s figure was measured before #56492 and is superseded.

There is no behaviour change with the flag at 1 (the default).
- The "profiling is disabled" warning now fires only when the flag is 0, graphs may be captured, and the extensible cache is off. It no longer suggests a `--gpu-memory-utilization` value, since that needed the skipped estimate.

## Validation

`test_cudagraph_memory_profile_runs_only_when_applied` covers MRV1, MRV2 with and without the extensible cache, and MRV2 without graphs. For each case it checks the estimate call, the KV cache budget and the warning.

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k cudagraph_memory_profile_runs_only_when_applied
7 passed                    # this PR (CPU)
3 failed, 4 passed          # main: all three flag-0 cases still run the estimate
3 failed, 4 passed          # previous revision of this PR: warns with the extensible cache on, and for MRV2 without graphs
```

CI runs this file in the H200 "V1 Executor + Worker" step (`pytest -v -s v1/worker`, `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`).

## Overview

**Split 1/5 of Kimi K3.1 (#65685): the model files.** Adds Kimi K3.1 (`KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration`) and its NVIDIA specialized decode under `vllm/models/kimi_k3`, plus the registry and renderer entries. Its `VerifyAndUpdateConfig` entry (the DSA kv-cache dtype defaults and dense drafts) comes with split 3/5.

This PR does not touch `vllm/v1/attention`. The KV cache and attention changes that K3.1 needs to serve come in split 3/5 (#66037). Until that lands, K3.1 imports but does not serve; Kimi-K3 keeps working.

| Split | PR | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 1/5 | this PR | Model files |
| 2/5 | #66028 | Rust renderer |
| 3/5 | #66037 | KV cache and attention changes to serve K3.1 at TP8 |
| 4/5 | #65685 | ROCm, P/D, indexer top-k backends |
| 5/5 | #66027 | DCP optimizations (opt-in), merged last |

## Claims

- **Kimi K3.1**:
  - Kimi-K3 with DSA (DeepSeek sparse attention) on every MLA layer (`dsa_config` in `KimiLinearConfig`).
  - DSA indexer kernels (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops`).
  - Packed KDA/DSA hybrid caches (`get_packed_hybrid_block_size`).
- **Drafts**: dense and GQA drafts for K3.1. Kimi-K3's `KimiK3MTPModel` stays.
- **Specialized decode** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode`):
  - CuTe DSL DSA (indexer, top-k exchange, sparse attention, DCP stage), KDA, MLA, MoE and GEMM kernels.
  - The drafter and recoverSSM.
  - Its DCP stage uses the packed top-k merge kernels, which live in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/dcp_topk_merge` here. Split 5/5 moves them to `vllm/v1/attention/ops` when the stock indexer uses them too.
  - It runs FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE through trtllm-gen only: the prims_ts, head padding and KV counter changes to that backend come with split 3/5 (#66037).
- **Python renderer**: K3.1 thinking efforts (low, medium, high, max).

## Validation

- Every NVIDIA/common module under `vllm.models.kimi_k3` imports on top of `main`'s shared code.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` hooks and the manual mypy hook pass on the changed files.
- Model tests and TP8 serving run on split 3/5, which adds the engine changes.

## Details

- `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration.process_weights_after_loading` was defined twice on the source branch, a merge leftover. commits.pr_title: [CI] Recompile the KV connector lock against the raised opentelemetry floors
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the CI image build on main, which fails at the KV connector `verify` step ([build 100662](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100662#01a1b271-bd32-4132-bd7b-9ac7e3888c38)):

```
filelock: image has 4.2.6, lock has 4.0.7
opentelemetry-api: image has 1.45.2, lock has 1.35.0
...
packaging: image has 26.3, lock has 24.2
lmcache requires opentelemetry-api<=1.40.0,>=1.20.0, but image has 1.45.2
lmcache requires opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus<=0.61b0,>=0.50b0, but image has 0.66b2
```

**Root cause:** a semantic conflict between two PRs.
- #63574 raised the security floors to `opentelemetry-* >= 1.45.1` and `filelock >= 4.2.4`, and updated `requirements/test/cuda.txt`.
- #65145 compiled `requirements/test/kv_connectors_cuda.txt` before #63574 landed.

Recompiling the lock alone fails. lmcache 0.5.6, and the latest 0.5.7 too, caps `opentelemetry-api<=1.40.0` and `opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus<=0.61b0`, so the lock can't be resolved against the new floors.

**Fix:**
- Add `requirements/test/kv_connectors_cuda.overrides`. It overrides lmcache's two opentelemetry caps when the lock is compiled, so the lock follows the image's pins from `test/cuda.txt`. The pre-commit `pip-compile-kv-connectors` hook passes it with `--override`.
- Allow those two `(lmcache, dep)` pairs in `ALLOWED_UNMET` in `tools/kv_connector_lock.py`. `verify` still checks every other requirement.
- Recompile the lock. filelock, packaging and the opentelemetry packages now match the image.

**Trade-off:** lmcache runs against opentelemetry 1.45 instead of its declared range of ≤1.40. The alternative is to keep vulnerable opentelemetry in the CI image. The LMCache connector jobs exercise this path.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `kv_connectors_cuda`.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` passes on the change, including `pip-compile-kv-connectors` and `check-kv-connector-lock`.
- `python tools/kv_connector_lock.py align`: OK.
- The CI image build on this PR exercises `plan` and `verify`.

- CI image build: pending.

commits.pr_title: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. The rest then has to be rescued one site at a time: buffers by name, and everything held some other way is lost. With this change `sleep(level=2)` states what the caller rewrites and keeps the rest, at the same address. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F11).

This replaces this PR's earlier site-by-site fixes (MXFP4 permute cache, DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load`, GEMM-RS/AR), which are reverted here because the rule covers them.

## Failures this addresses

All come from non-parameter state in the weights pool. Measured on GB200 without any fix:

| State | How it is held | Failure after a level-2 wake |
|---|---|---|
| GEMM-RS/AR peer pointer table from `symm_mem.rendezvous` | Inside the torch handle | Table reads all zeros, then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` on the first forward. Kimi-K3 placeholder weights, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with GEMM-RS |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load` indices | Weight loader closure | GSM8K 0.90 → 0.0, and later reloads don't repair it |
| MXFP4 TRT-LLM permute cache | Quant method attribute | gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.375 → 0.0 |

The same pattern is in code but not measured: Inkling and Beam peer tables, DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram handles (#64922), plain attributes (#60009), attention impl state (#62634).

## Change

- `CuMemAllocator.sleep` and `XpuMemAllocator.sleep` take `discardable`: a weights allocation is discarded only if every live block in it starts at an address in `discardable`. An address that doesn't match keeps the allocation, so a wrong match costs host memory, not state.
- `Worker.sleep(level=2)` passes the storage addresses of the parameters the update rewrites, through `SleepModeBackend.suspend(discardable)`. That replaces `level`, which said the same thing: nothing discardable is level 1. It changes a plugin interface, so an out-of-tree backend must follow.

Kept tensors stay in `weights` and return on `wake_up(["weights"])`, so tags keep their meaning. Level 1 is unchanged.

## Removed

These existed to survive level 2, which now keeps them:

- Model state in the runtime pool (#63548), LoRA state in the runtime pool (#62358), and the MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill workspace in the runtime pool (#64856). All three are built during `load_model`; none is a parameter.
- The CPU copies of `named_buffers()`, on every platform.
- The separate CPU save and restore of `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`. Preserved parameters are now just not discardable, so their backup goes through the allocator: pinned where `PIN_MEMORY` is on, instead of pageable, and kept across wake for reuse.

Left in place: buffers registered for this reason (they are still correct as buffers), and the KV-init and CUDA graph runtime pools, which are outside `load_model`.

## Not covered

- Parameters the update doesn't write, such as those absent from the checkpoint: still discarded, as today. `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` is for those.
- `discard(tags)`: unchanged. Its only caller passes `kv_cache`.
- Weight-derived tensors that post-load processing doesn't refresh now keep old values instead of garbage. That is a separate bug class.


## Validation

Every run is the RL cycle: `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`. Nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions unless noted. Code at 33056538ad and e82bcb85c4; later commits change only docs and comments and merge main.

**Weights over NCCL, through the state-transition verifier.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, TP4, 2 updates, every tensor sent except the Engram embedding tables. The fixed-token oracle compares logprobs before and after.

| Code | GSM8K before → after | Oracle | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9007 → **0.0** | Differs | 28331 |
| Earlier site-by-site fixes | 0.9045 → 0.9037 | Same | 28323 |
| | 0.9030 → 0.9067 | Same | 28329 |
| This PR | 0.9067 → 0.8923 | Same | 28322 |
| | 0.9022 → 0.9098 | Same | 28327 |
| | 0.9007 → 0.8984 | Same | 28328 |

Across the three runs of this PR GSM8K moves -1.44, +0.76 and -0.23 points. The noise between identical runs here is about 1.5 points.

**Reload from disk**, GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 3 cycles. "Differing" compares tensors per rank with a real cold start.

| Model | Code | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | This PR, real start | 0.9052 → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| | This PR, dummy start | — → 0.9030 → 0.9014 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | main | 0.9022 → **0.0** → **0.0** | 160 / 160 experts | 46346 |
| | This PR | 0.9083 → 0.8976 → 0.8931 | 0 / 160 experts | 46345 |
| Beam NVFP4 | main | 0.9431, then **hangs**: `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` | — | 46339 |
| | This PR | 0.9447 → 0.9439 → 0.9454 | 0 / 1224 all parameters | 46338 |
| MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 | main | 0.166 → 0.166 → 0.190 | 0 / 2150 all parameters | 46337 |
| | This PR | 0.175 → 0.187 → 0.178 | 0 / 2150 all parameters | 46336 |
| Kimi-K3 8-layer placeholder, GEMM-AR on | main | Illegal address on the first forward | — | 46016 |
| | This PR | Values are fake, so not meaningful | 0 / 358 all parameters | 46268 |

The dummy start is also an update between different weights: state derived from random weights would stay stale and lower GSM8K. MiniMax-M3 scores low on main too, so its run only shows no regression from removing the MSA runtime pool. The Beam hang is one run per arm, and its cause isn't diagnosed.

**LoRA with no reload, the flows #62358 fixed.** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with a real adapter, GB300, TP 1 and 2, waking all at once or weights before KV cache, 2 cycles. Output compared token by token with before sleep, with and without the adapter. `inplace` preserves nothing and has user code write every parameter back.

| Code | `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]` | `inplace` | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | Same | Same | 28336 |
| This PR | Same | Same | 28334 |
| Negative control: this PR, discarding the whole weights pool | Same | **Differs**, 4 of 4 | 28335 |

**ROCm,** MI355X, reload from disk, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, 3 cycles: this PR 0.9469 → 0.9477 → 0.9500 (34144), main 0.9500 → 0.9492 → 0.9500 (34145). That path doesn't hit the failures above on main, so this shows no regression and that the pool snapshot works on ROCm. `test_cumem.py` 22 passed, and `test_sleep_mode.py -k deep_sleep` 9 passed (34143).

**What level 2 backs up to host memory,** per rank:

| Model | GPU memory freed | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 80.35 GiB | 0.97 GiB | 2.35 GiB |
| Beam NVFP4 | 70.15 GiB | 0.39 GiB | 1.55 GiB |
| Kimi-K3 placeholder | 34.94 GiB | 0.30 GiB | 1.14 GiB |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MI355X | 40.81 GiB | 0.10 GiB | 1.87 GiB |

**Tests,** GB200 and GB300, 2 GPUs: `test_cumem.py` 22 passed; `test_sleep_mode.py` and `test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py` 20 passed, 1 skipped, including LoRA and the multimodal models; `tests/lora` manager, worker and layers 263 passed, 168 skipped; `tests/v1/worker` and the MiniMax-M3 MSA kernel tests 115 passed, 3 skipped. `test_level2_keeps_what_the_update_does_not_rewrite` and `test_deep_sleep_keeps_preserved_parameters` are new. The backup check in `test_cumem.py` is updated for what level 2 now keeps.

**Not run:** XPU, full Kimi-K3, Inkling and MiniMax-M3 at the verifier level. AMD CI is blocked waiting for approval. The `sleep_mode.md` section was read cold by an agent twice and corrected from what it couldn't answer.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix tkw1 rejecting count-free expert metadata, rename AITER QuantMethod
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #63204 (part of #54966 item 5), addressing its post-merge review comments.

## Claims

- **Fix:** `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` again accepts expert-token metadata without token counts on the tkw1 route (e.g. DeepEP v2 under CUDA graphs). #63204 made the check reject *any* metadata; it now rejects only metadata that carries counts, as before. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447566182))
- **Rename:** `QuantMethod` → `AiterQuantType` (plus `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE`, `quant_type=`, `derive_aiter_quant_type()`), since "quant method" means the weight-loading quantization classes in vLLM. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447852851))
- **Removal:** `ActivationMethod`. It only named SILU/GELU; every activation now resolves via `rocm_aiter_ops.get_aiter_activation_type()`, as SWIGLU/SITU already did. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447841385))
- **Guard:** assert `a1q_scale is None` on the tkw1 branch. tkw1 quantizes the activation itself, so a dispatch-side scale would be silently dropped where the generic route forwards it.
- No numerical change intended.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 88 passed |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k aiter` | 67 passed, 14 skipped |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py` | 53 passed |

The new regression test was mutation-checked against both ways the fix can regress:

| Mutation | Failure |
|---|---|
| revert the fix (reject any metadata) | `AssertionError: AITER tkw1 kernel does not support num_local_tokens` |
| let count-free metadata fall through to the generic route | `count-free metadata did not reach the tkw1 kernel` |

The second is why the test spies on `rocm_aiter_ops.asm_moe_tkw1` rather than only comparing outputs: `asm_moe_tkw1` is `fused_moe(quant_type=per_Token, doweight_stage1=True)`, so the generic route is numerically equivalent and an output-only check passes through a fall-through.

## Details

- Output comparison uses `rtol=atol=1e-2`: tkw1 differs by ~1 bf16 ulp run to run. The test is gated on gfx942/gfx950, like the other asm/FP8 tests in the file.
- The enum-value test now checks `AiterQuantType` against `aiter.QuantType` rather than literals, so drift from AITER is caught.
- The mirror enum is kept because subclasses declare `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE` at class definition, in a module imported where AITER isn't installed.
- Raw custom-op tests now pass AITER's own `ActivationType`/`QuantType`.
- `rocm_aiter_ops` custom-op argument names (`quant_method: int`, `activation_method: int`) are unchanged: they are `torch.ops.vllm.*` schema names, so renaming them is a schema change rather than a Python rename. Out-of-tree callers of `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` must rename `quant_method=` to `quant_type=`.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these names or the tkw1 check.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Keep nightlies off PR-writable images and trim the csrc cache key
commits.pr_body:
- `build.sh`: nightlies and branch builds reuse only `rocm/vllm-ci` images and cache, never read back `rocm/vllm-dev`, and write no cache of their own
- `build.sh`: the trust comment says the `pr<N>-`/`br-` prefixes keep names apart but isolate nothing, and that the per-commit test image is still pulled by tag
- `Dockerfile.rocm`: a new `csrc-inputs` stage hands the csrc compile only what `setup.py` reads from `pyproject.toml` and `envs.py`, and fails the build if the filtered `envs.py` would change a value `setup.py` reads
- `test_rocm_build.py`: only PR builds read back their own namespace, and nightlies still reuse `rocm/vllm-ci` images and cache

Every untrusted build pushes with the same `rocm/vllm-dev` credentials, so any PR could plant the `br-` images or cache an AITER nightly would reuse. Nightlies now take only what `rocm/vllm-ci` has. When a nightly's stack or runtime key is main's and CI has not pushed it yet, it waits for main's build of it (#63949) and builds it itself only if none is running; a branch whose stack or runtime inputs differ from main's now rebuilds them on every build. The nightly's per-commit test image is still pulled from `rocm/vllm-dev` by tag, and PR builds share the agents' buildkitd cache mounts with trusted builds as before, so both are left for ci-infra. Separately, 67 of the 240 commits on main that changed a csrc input over the last 60 days touched only `pyproject.toml` or `envs.py`, and each one recompiled all HIP code; replayed through the new filter, none of them changes the csrc inputs anymore. Follow-up to #61939; with main (and #63949) merged in, `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` passes 41 tests in 10 runs out of 10.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Fix/spec decode insert resampled race
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Run `_insert_resampled_kernel` with `num_warps=1` to avoid a race when reading and updating `num_sampled` in place. The race can cause an out-of-range lookup during speculative decoding and a fatal CUDA exception.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-warp read/write race in `_insert_resampled_kernel` by restricting its execution to one warp.
- Changes only this kernel's launch configuration.
- Makes no performance or model-quality claims.

## Validation

Two CUDA core dumps from separate crashes on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell show the same failure mechanism:

| Incident | Threads reading `num_sampled = 4` | Threads reading `num_sampled = 5` |
|---|---|---|
| First | 0, 32 | 64, 96 |
| Second | 0, 32, 64 | 96 |

The listed threads represent different warps within the same block. Disassembly maps these values to the load of `num_sampled`; the corresponding resampling indices are 4 and 5, with an exclusive end index of 5.

Both dumps report `Warp Out of range Address` at `_insert_resampled_kernel+384`, corresponding to:

    temp = tl.load(temp_ptr + req_state_idx).to(tl.float32)

The failing environment used vLLM 0.32.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, and Gemma 4 MTP with four speculative tokens. The same read/update pattern remains in the main-branch code patched here.

Local validation:
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, typos, and repository Python checks.
- Python syntax validation and `git diff --check` passed.

The dumps establish the original failure mechanism.

## Details

The kernel loads `num_sampled`, uses it to compute a resampling index, and increments the same counter in global memory. In the captured machine code, there is no inter-warp barrier between the load and the store.

A delayed warp can therefore read the incremented value after another warp has performed the update. In both incidents, this changes the resampling index from 4 to 5, outside the request's logits range. The subsequent mapping lookup supplies an invalid request-state index, causing the temperature load to fault.

Using one warp removes this inter-warp dependency without changing the sampling algorithm or introducing another kernel launch.

This failure occurs before the NaN/argmax handling addressed by #50183.

## Overview

Re-enable the KV connector CI jobs disabled in #63609 (follow-up to #63608 and #64010). Instead of installing NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake and CuPy at job time, the CUDA 13 CI image now bakes them from a hash-pinned lock.

At build time it adds 16 packages and changes none already in the image.
- `install-kv-connectors.sh` becomes `check-kv-connectors.sh`. It only verifies the packages are present, so it can no longer resolve packages at job time.
- **ROCm needs no image change.** `kv_connectors_rocm.txt` (`tblib`, `lm_eval[api]`) is fully covered by `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, so the runtime installs were no-ops. They and the file are removed.
- **26 job blocks re-enabled.** The CUDA and AMD jobs are listed in the build below.
- **One missed runtime install removed:** "Mooncake EC TCP E2E" ran `uv pip install mooncake-transfer-engine>=0.3.12` into a venv. It now uses the image's Mooncake through `--system-site-packages`.
- 6 tethering-allowlist entries removed.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on all changed files passed: pip-compile-kv-connectors, shellcheck, step keys, test tethering (`--all` reports nothing stale) and Dockerfile graph.
- All Buildkite YAML parses. Each restored block matches its pre-#63609 definition except for the script rename and the dropped ROCm install line.
- Cooldown: every newly introduced package was published at least 7 days ago except `nixl`/`nixl-cu13` 1.5.2 (PyPI Oct 29). Main already pins it in `requirements/kv_connectors.txt` since #64585. **Please don't merge before Nov 5** if we hold to the 7-day rule.
- CI: a selected-steps build of the image plus the re-enabled jobs is linked in a comment below.

## Details

- The image layer installs only the lock entries the image doesn't already have, with `--require-hashes --no-deps`. It fails the build if the install changed any preinstalled package. After the vLLM and EP kernel wheels are installed, `tools/kv_connector_lock.py verify` fails the build if any locked package differs from its locked version or has unmet requirements. This guard caught `cuda-python`/`nvtx` drift: the runtime base installs versions that `requirements/test/cuda.txt` doesn't pin. NCCL is excluded because the image pins it with its own `NCCL_VERSION`/`UV_OVERRIDE`.
- **Scope:** only the stable x86_64 CUDA 13 image. Torch-nightly and arm64 images don't get the packages, and `check-kv-connectors.sh` fails fast there with a clear message. The KV jobs only run on x86 L4/H100/H200/B200 pools.

  - The two Intel jobs that `pip install -r requirements/kv_connectors.txt` on the XPU image. They need an Intel image change.

commits.pr_title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Fix mixed draft-model warmup token budget
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Draft-model initialization with speculative decoding can fail during mixed prefill/decode warmup:
```
AssertionError: Shape: 2050 out of considered ranges: [(1, 2048)]
```

The warmup creates one synthetic decode request and one synthetic prefill request, but builds the scheduler inputs directly and bypasses the scheduler's correction-slot reservation. The extra query slots for these requests were missing from the warmup token budget, allowing the resulting shape to exceed max_num_tokens.

When a speculator is enabled, cap the warmup token count at max_num_tokens - num_warmup_reqs * num_extra_query_per_req. Skip the warmup if the adjusted budget is too small for a mixed step.

This fixes a regression in the mixed warmup path added by [#56492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Pair P/D blocks by the last token with different block sizes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With different P/D block sizes, NIXL pull pairs D's and P's block lists by position, so KV lands in the wrong blocks, or D crashes, when the two lists start or end at different tokens. This pairs them by the request's last token and rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes.

## Claims

- With different P/D block sizes, D receives every page into the right block, also after a partial prefix hit on D or sliding-window clipping.
- Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) land in the right blocks too, and D's EngineCore no longer dies on `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`.
- DCP across different P/D logical block sizes is rejected at the handshake.
- Pulls between equal P/D block sizes are unchanged.
- Without `remote_num_tokens`, pulls between different P/D block sizes fail instead of pairing by position, with an error logged once per remote engine.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "hetero_ppl or dcp"
```

`_run_hetero_case` now passes `remote_num_tokens`, the hetero-ppl sweep and `test_hetero_ppl_with_block_size_ratio` gain a pure-MLA row (the latter with a 2-block hit on D), and `test_dcp_rejects_different_logical_block_sizes` covers the DCP guard. `test_hetero_ppl_pull_without_remote_num_tokens_fails` covers the failed pull, and `test_dcp_pull_with_block_size_ratio_writes_stay_within_request_blocks` DCP reads between different kernel block sizes.

CPU, this PR at `4524ec3cdc` on main `8530a778f7`: 44 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>CPU output</summary>

```
# main 8530a778f7 + this PR's tests
44 failed, 182 passed, 106 deselected
  34 TOKEN MISALIGNMENT, 8 assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group), 1 DID NOT RAISE NotImplementedError, 1 READ posted without remote_num_tokens
# this PR 4524ec3cdc
226 passed, 106 deselected
```

</details>

GB10 (setup as in #58860): with this PR, every case below gives logprobs bitwise equal to matched-block P/D, and gpt-oss-20b with FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128, no longer kills D's EngineCore.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

main `8530a778f7`, without and with this PR at `0afbebd9e0`. Identical texts vs the matched-block P/D run on the same image (D's block size on both sides; for TRITON_ATTN, whose prefill tile follows the block size, P's):

| case | without | with, logprobs bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 16/64 | 4/7 | 7/7 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), 544/1088, 1088-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |

gpt-oss-20b, FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128 kills D's EngineCore on main (`assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`) and runs with this PR.

</details>

## Details

With different P/D block sizes:

1. P's scheduler returns its block ids and `remote_num_tokens` in `kv_transfer_params`, with the sliding-window blocks that left the window dropped.
2. D's scheduler hands NIXL its block ids past a local prefix hit, window-clipped the same way. The hit and the clipping start the two lists at different tokens, and each side pads to its own logical block past the last token.
3. D's pull pairs each group's block lists by position: `_map_block_ids_for_block_size_ratio` front-clips D's sub-blocks to P's count, then `_apply_prefix_caching` end-trims P to D's count. That holds only if both lists start and end at the same token, which step 2 breaks. Pages then land one or more blocks off.
4. D's receive post-process zeroes the sub-blocks the read did not cover.

Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) shift pages the same way; when D's padded list is longer than P's, D's read fails `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)` and its EngineCore dies.

This drops each side's padding past the last of the `remote_num_tokens` that P already sends and pairs the lists backwards from there, once per request in `_read_blocks_for_req`. `ReqMeta.covered_sub_blocks` lets the receive post-process zero exactly what P doesn't send: D's padding, and D's leading sub-blocks when D's sliding window starts before P's.

Without `remote_num_tokens`, which a router may not forward, D can't find the last token, so the pull fails. P's block size is only known after the handshake, so the scheduler can't decline the request earlier.

DCP reads keep positional pairing, which needs equal logical block sizes because each side shards tokens at its own. They are mapped to remote-sized sub-blocks in `_read_blocks_for_req` too, so `_read_blocks` no longer maps block ids.

#51527 (draft) lets Mamba hybrids with different logical but equal kernel block sizes use prefix caching, pairing their full-attention groups from new scheduler metadata; it leaves the attention-only end-trim and the `block_size_ratio > 1` pairing fixed here unchanged. #60483 (draft) rejects different P/D DCP sizes when `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` differs from the block size; this PR rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes. #60484 rejects DCP peers with different interleave sizes; since NIXL sets the interleave to the block size by default, that overlaps this PR's DCP guard when both sides use DCP.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER's all-gather for small TP all-gathers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm gfx950 and gfx942, TP all-gathers now use AITER's IPC all-gather instead of RCCL when the TP group already runs AITER custom all-reduce. "Small" means fp32/fp16/bf16 at TP 2, 4 or 8, up to AITER's own per-rank limit (`should_custom_ag`: vLLM's 128 MiB AITER buffer / (2 x TP) = 32 / 16 / 8 MiB). vLLM adds no cap of its own: in two AITER vs RCCL sweeps, no timed size (TP2: up to 20 of its 32 MiB) was faster on RCCL in both runs. gfx1250 stays on RCCL until it is measured; gfx942 was verified by @frida-andersson on MI325X ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082), Claims). This extends #48247 (DP only) to TP. #48446's RCCL path stays as the fallback. Below, `base` is a main-equivalent image, `pr` adds the previous head's files (b8fd6897a0, with a 2 MiB cap) and `r1` adds 1eb0aa0805's: the round-1 code with a gfx950-only gate, called "this head" below. The current head, 8ca2504b97, is that code rebased onto main with the gate widened to gfx942; it routes gfx950 the same way. See the image table under GPU. cN means N requests in flight.

## Claims

- **Decode step 1.2-1.9% faster at TP4 c1-c4 (4 swapped rounds), 1.4% at TP4 c8 (one swapped pair) and 0.8-1.2% at TP8 c1-c4** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X; `base` matches main on the touched files).
  - TP4 `--monokernel`, previous head, 4 position-swapped rounds (P1-P4): -106 / -120 / -102 us at c1 / c2 / c4 (-1.94 / -1.79 / -1.19%). pr was faster in all 12 round and concurrency pairs, and each drop exceeds the largest same-arm, same-half spread (15 / 27 / 77 us). This head routes c1-c4 decode the same way (every decode gather there is at most 1.81 MB per rank, under the old cap). A c1 re-run on the rebased head gives -113 us against base (previous head: -106 us) and -12 us against pr.
  - TP4 c8 / c16 / c32, this head, where the logits gathers (3.1-14.5 MB per rank) now move to AITER. Against base (one swapped pair, R1/R2): -185 / -350 / -133 us (-1.41 / -2.11 / -0.65%). Against pr (R3/R4, the cap removal alone): -83 / -52 / -307 us. Together they imply pr - base of -102 us at c8, in line with P1-P4 (-106 us at c1), but -298 / +174 us at c16 / c32, where pr differs from base only by Engram gathers. So about 200 us of between-round drift sits in c16 and c32, and neither is established. c8 holds in all four orientations but is marginal: against base, R1's -121 us is just above r1's 116 us same-half spread and inside the cell's largest rep range (145 us); against pr, both orientations (-77 / -89 us) are inside the spread.
  - TP8 without `--monokernel`, previous head (T1-T4: base, pr, pr, base): -0.81 / -1.11 / -1.24% at c1 / c2 / c4, each above the same-arm spread across server starts (21 / 6 / 54 us). The routing there is unchanged; not re-run.
  - Always copying in, instead of AITER's registered capture path (scratch mutant `mut_reg`, M1/M2), costs about 25 us per step at c1, about a quarter of the c1 gain.
  - Under the torch profiler, pr's TP4 step was slower at c1 and c2; without it, pr and r1 were faster than base in every run (see Tradeoffs).
- **gfx942 (MI325X), verified by @frida-andersson** ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082)), with the gate widened to gfx942. The cell is TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32768 -> 1024, 32 prompts, c1. ITL p50 went 7.15 -> 7.01 ms (-140 us) on the same 4 GPUs and 7.04 -> 6.99 ms (-50 us) on different GPU halves: two passes, not position-swapped. TTFT and TPOT were flat, and `niah_single_2` at 16384 scored 1.0. Not measured on gfx942: c2 and up (including the c8+ gathers above the old 2 MiB cap) and the AITER vs RCCL sweep.
- **AITER never lost to RCCL in both of two sweeps** (TP 2/4/8, 768 timed points each; table below). The sweeps cover 1 KiB up to AITER's limit (TP2: up to 20 MiB of its 32), dims 0 / middle / last, bf16 and fp32, eager and graph replay, all bit-exact against RCCL. The better run is at least 1.07x at every point. Run 1 alone lost at 13 points (down to 0.32x, TP2 graph, 2.004 MiB), each at least 1.21x in run 2. Dim 0 (a copy-in plus AITER's kernel against one RCCL kernel) has graph-replay medians of 1.18 / 1.41 / 1.43x at TP 2/4/8 and lost only in run 1 (5 graph points of 128 KiB or less), so it stays on AITER.
- **Bit-exact gathers; GSM8K accuracy unchanged; acceptance length (AL) has no consistent direction.** The PR's GPU test checks TP2 with `torch.equal`, eager and under graph replay; scratch matrices extend this to TP4 and TP8 and up to AITER's limit. On GSM8K-1319 (6 base-vs-PR pairs of the same pass), mean accuracy is 0.916 on both arms, and the per-question flips between arms (68-82) are about the same as within one arm (63-81). AL changed by +0.005, -0.010, -0.021 and -0.055 with pr on half B, and by -0.005, +0.013, +0.027 and -0.014 with r1 on half A. Only the -0.055 (GSM8K-300 with expandable segments, E1, one unswapped run) exceeds every same-arm AL span (at most 0.030). The +0.027 (r1, 16 in flight, no same-condition repeat) exceeds every same-condition span (at most 0.024), but not base's 0.030 across 4/16/32 in flight. The perf tables use synthetic AL 3.87.
- **No change elsewhere.** CUDA, ROCm archs other than gfx950 and gfx942, ROCm without `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, non-TP groups, TP6 and gate rejects keep their current path. No new flag. GPU-checked on gfx950: gate rejects, the DP group and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0`. The arch gate rests on a CPU probe.
- **Not claimed:** gfx1250 (gated off, not tested); gfx942 beyond the reviewer's two c1 passes (no sweep, no c2+, no swapped rounds); other models; timing at TP2 between 20 and 32 MiB per rank (bit-exact in the matrix, not timed). The earlier stack-image result (-2.2% to -2.6% at c1, with 5 other PRs) is context only (see Runs and noise).

## Validation

**CPU** (this head unless noted)
- [x] `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py::test_rocm_tp_all_gather_uses_aiter` (default L4 and MI300 "Distributed Comm Ops" steps): 7/7 pass (whole file: 39 passed, 10 skipped for GPUs). Dropping the `should_custom_ag` check fails exactly the rejection case. A gate widened to gfx1250 (`get_cdna_version() >= 3`) still passes, because the mock sets `use_aiter_tp_all_gather` directly. On the previous head, main's communicator failed the dim-0, middle-dim and last-dim cases, and dropping any one of the TP-size, 16-byte-row, non-empty or 2-D-view checks failed exactly one case (output below).
- [x] Arch-gate probe (scratch; vLLM's own gate inputs, arch faked). AITER all-reduce is enabled only on gfx942, gfx950 and gfx1250, at CDNA versions 3 / 4 / 5. So `in (3, 4)` is true on gfx942 and gfx950 only, and false on gfx90a, gfx908, gfx1250, gfx1100, gfx1201 and non-ROCm. The probe ran for the previous gate (`== 4`); the new result follows from the same logged inputs.
- [x] Emulation against AITER v0.1.26's index math, previous head: 35/35 (c1 call sites at TP2/4/8; int64, uint8, non-contiguous, unaligned rows, empty, 6 GPUs, non-TP group, AITER off).
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on the 4 changed files.

**GPU** (MI355X gfx950, AITER 0.1.26). Every gain credited to the PR compares `pr` or `r1` with `base`, except the cap-removal numbers (`r1` against `pr`) and the sweep (AITER against RCCL inside one image); `revcomm` and `mut_reg` check only the tests and the design.

| Image | Contents | Produced | Credited to the PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5, unchanged; touched files equal main 41f5146b5b | the reference arm of P1-P4, T1-T4, R1/R2 and every accuracy run | reference |
| `pr` | base + the previous head's two files (2 MiB cap, no arch gate) | P1-P4, T1-T4, Q1/S1/E1, profile, sync check, R3/R4; the sweep (cap lifted in the benchmark, so it times this head's path) | TP4/TP8 c1-c4, accuracy at 4 in flight, sweep |
| `r1` | base + this head's two files (gfx950 gate, no cap) | R1-R4, RQ, this head's GPU tests and matrix | TP4 c8 (c16/c32 not established), the c1 re-run, GSM8K at 4/16/32 in flight |
| `revcomm` (scratch) | base + only the previous head's `aiter_custom_all_reduce.py` (this head's but for a docstring); main's `cuda_communicator.py` | the new GPU test fails | no: shows that the test detects the change |
| `mut_reg` (scratch) | pr with `all_gather_unreg` replaced by AITER's registered capture path | M1/M2 copy-in cost; the expandable-segments failure | no: tests the copy-in design |

- [x] `test_rocm_aiter_tp_all_gather` (2 GPUs) passes on r1 and pr, also with expandable segments. With the current gate, it asserts that AITER ran dims `[0, 0, -1, -1, -1, -1]` on gfx942 and gfx950, and that AITER never ran on gfx1250, where AITER all-reduce also starts. It has run only on gfx950.
- [x] **Fails without the change:** on `revcomm` it fails at `assert aiter_dims == expected_dims` (line 196), after every `torch.equal` check passed.
- [x] `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py`: 4 passed on r1, pr and base. In a probe on pr, AITER-on engines took the new path and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` engines stayed on RCCL, with equal greedy output.
- [x] **Gate matrix on r1** (scratch): 79 cases at TP2/4/8, plus TP2/4 with expandable segments; 0 failures. Contiguous cases are bit-exact, eager and under replay. The old cap plus one row and AITER's exact limit go to AITER; the limit plus 16 B or one row, 24-byte rows, non-16-byte totals and int32 go to RCCL. Non-contiguous inputs and the DP group stay on RCCL.
- [x] **The registered capture path fails where copy-in passes:** `mut_reg` raises "a collective buffer cannot be IPC-exported" on the TP2 matrix with expandable segments.
- [x] TP2xPP2 (`test_multi_process_tensor_parallel_pipeline_parallel[test_target3-2-2]`): passes on pr (gathers on AITER) and base.
- [x] AITER vs RCCL sweep at TP2/4/8, run twice.
- [x] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: P1-P4, T1-T4, M1/M2 and 4 GSM8K/AL runs on pr; R1-R4 and GSM8K-1319 at 4/16/32 in flight (RQ) on r1.
- [x] On pr: profile (all 6 RCCL gathers per TP4 decode step moved to AITER at c1/c2/c4), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (0 sync errors), and E1 with expandable segments (started, captured, served, ran GSM8K-300).
- [x] 0 Traceback, RuntimeError, EngineDeadError, MEMORY_FAULT or HSA_STATUS_ERROR lines in 34 server logs (24 from the previous-head rounds, 10 from this round), and 0 failed requests out of the 2048 in R1-R4.
- [ ] *Partial:* #48446's TP8 c4 TPOT benchmark, with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash standing in for DeepSeek-V4: one server start per arm, -0.63% mean TPOT, not established.

**Not covered**

<details>
<summary>Profile (pr, c1-c4): gathers moved, and why the profiled step was slower</summary>

**Gathers moved** (TP4, torch-profiler window on the accuracy servers, ranks 0 and 3; torch profiler on rocprofiler-sdk, not `rocprofv3`). Profiled steps run slower than un-profiled ones, so only counts and kernel times are used here. All six RCCL gathers per step move to AITER at c1, c2 and c4:
- two in each of the two Engram layers: rows along dim 1, and the `wkv` `gather_output` along dim -1;
- the target logits gather (eager);
- the draft logits gather (draft graph).

None of them is a dim-0 gather. Main's `wkv` gather, which the earlier stack image did not have, is now measured.

| Concurrency | base: RCCL gather + `movedim`, us/step | pr: copy-in + AITER gather, us/step | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 161.9 | 79.1 | -82.8 us |
| 2 | 174.2 | 100.3 | -73.9 us |
| 4 | 217.8 | 139.3 | -78.5 us |

- **Kernel count.** Kernels per step are unchanged (410 / 416 / 418). The 6 copy-ins take 28.5-29.8 us per step.
- **Host path.** The eager logits gather drops from 12 HIP calls (159-280 us of host time, profiled) to 2 (66-82 us). That may account for the rest of the c1 gain.
- **TP8 without `--monokernel`.** About 6 gathers per decode step move (5 graph-replayed, 1 eager, the same split as the six TP4 sites; not traced to call sites): 809 RCCL `ddaAllGatherIpc` kernels become 809 AITER `allgather_lastdim` kernels per c1 window (ranks 0 and 7); on rank 0, 800 of them fall in the window's 134 decode steps (~6 per step). The 180 RCCL kernels in the 4 prefill chunks are the same in both arms.

**Why the profiled TP4 step was slower.** In the target graph, 4 RCCL kernels plus 4 `movedim` kernels become 4 AITER kernels plus 4 memcpy nodes. Both arms have 206 nodes; pr has 8 memcpy nodes instead of 4. The draft graph goes from 7 memcpy nodes to 8.
- **Profiled steps.** Under the torch profiler, pr's step was slower at c1 (8024 vs 6930 us) and c2 (7913 vs 7180 us), and faster at c4 (9008 vs 9160 us). Without the profiler, the same two servers ran pr faster at c1 (ITL p50 5.415 vs 5.541 ms, 2 requests). This TP4 profile is not swapped (pr on half B).
- **Where the time went (c1).** pr's rank 3 started its steps a median 6.9 ms after the earliest rank and was last at the first all-reduce in 362 of 392 steps. Base's ranks 3 and 0 were also late (5.9 and 5.3 ms; rank 3 last in 267 of 413 steps), so lateness alone does not explain the difference. On rank 3, where the GPU waited for the launch in both arms, the target graph's `hipGraphLaunch` call took a median 874 us on pr against 687 us on base, and the median idle inside the graph was 753 us against 0.2 us. In the median-length step the call lasted 815 us on pr and 825 us on base: base's GPU spent it in a 1016 us all-reduce wait, while pr's ran the graph's first 8 nodes, then idled 743 us until the call returned.
- **Ranks 0-2.** pr's call took 1280-1333 us against 664-728 us on base, but there the host ran ahead (rank 0: the first graph kernel started 5848 us after the call began, against 50 us on base), so the longer call likely includes queue backpressure. It cost nothing: on rank 0 the median idle inside the graph was 0.2 us.
- **c2 and c4.** At c2, pr's late rank called `hipGraphLaunch` a median 340 us after its GPU started the step; base's called it 2.9 ms before. At c4 the host led by 6.6-7.2 ms in both arms.
- **TP8** (one server, no halves): profiled c1 ITL p50 was 30.31-30.74 ms on base and 30.74-30.85 ms on pr (2 requests each): at most 0.5 ms slower (0.27 ms in the mean), against +1.0 ms at TP4 (profiled c1 ITL p50 6.92 vs 7.94 ms).
- **Reading.** The longer launch call costs step time only when the host is on the critical path; the profiler slows the host and puts it there at TP4 c1 and c2. Without the profiler, removing the copy-in nodes (M1/M2) saves 25 us at c1, not the ~1 ms the profiled step suggests.
</details>

Server, TP4. There is one instance per 4-GPU half (`ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3` and `4,5,6,7`), and both were benchmarked at the same time:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size 1 --monokernel \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --block-size 128 \
  --moe-backend aiter --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --language-model-only \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

Variants of that server:
- **Accuracy, profile, sync, E1 and RQ rounds:** `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` without the synthetic AL.
- **Profile round:** adds `--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/trace/...","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'`.
- **Sync round:** adds `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- **E1:** adds `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`; c1/c2/c4 x 8 prompts (512 out), then salted GSM8K-300.
- **M1/M2:** the perf recipe, with `mut_reg` in place of base.
- **R1-R4:** the perf recipe at c1, c8, c16 and c32.
- **TP8:** the same server with `--tensor-parallel-size 8` on all 8 GPUs and no `--monokernel`.
- **#48446-style TP8 rounds:** no `--speculative-config`, plus `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

Benchmark. Warm-up first (P rounds: c4 x 8 prompts; R rounds: c32 x 64 prompts; TP8: c2 x 4 prompts; all 32k in / 256 out, seed 7; #48446-style rounds: c4 x 8 prompts, 8k in / 128 out), then:

```bash
for r in 1 2; do for c in 1 2 4; do   # R rounds: for c in 1 8 16 32
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts 32 \
  --seed $((100 + c)) --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
done; done
# #48446-style: --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 32 --seed 481 / 482
# no-spec sweep: --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --max-concurrency $c --num-prompts max(16, 4c) --seed $((300 + c))
```

Accuracy: GSM8K over `/v1/completions`, with the prompt, stops and scoring of sglang's `few_shot_gsm8k`: 8 shots, the first 1319 (or 300) test questions, temperature 0, at most 512 new tokens, `--parallel 4` (RQ also 16 and 32). GSM8K-1319 runs once cold and once with a per-request `cache_salt`; GSM8K-300 and RQ's 16 and 32 passes are salted.
</details>

## Details

**Motivation.** #48446 kept ROCm TP all-gathers on RCCL (the pynccl + `movedim` path was slower), and #48247 enabled AITER's all-gather for DP only. Latency-bound decode gathers, such as the `LogitsProcessor` logits gather and DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram gathers, still pay an RCCL launch plus a `movedim` copy when dim != 0. Models have added their own AITER gather helpers (#57832, #63263, #63322, and #60606 for the DCP group). This PR moves TP gathers in the communicator instead; it does not replace those helpers, whose int64, above-limit and DCP-group gathers stay outside its gate.

**Design** (`CudaCommunicator._aiter_all_gather`, inside the existing ROCm branch):
- **Gate:** `use_aiter_tp_all_gather`, set once in `__init__`, is `use_aiter_allreduce` (TP only) and `get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)` (gfx942, gfx950). Per call: TP 2, 4 or 8 (AITER all-reduce allows 6, but its all-gather launches nothing there); bf16/fp16/fp32; non-empty and contiguous; and `should_custom_ag` accepts it (a multiple of 16 bytes, at most 32 / 16 / 8 MiB per rank at TP 2/4/8). Anything else goes to RCCL. Only arch, dtype, shape and contiguity decide, so all ranks agree.
- **Any dim.** A later dim runs as a last-dim gather of the 2-D view `(-1, prod(shape[dim:]))`, with no `movedim` copy. The row must be a whole number of 16-byte packs.
- **Always copy-in (`all_gather_unreg`), also under capture.** Persistent TP inputs such as Engram `staged_rows` may not be IPC-exportable (for example, with expandable segments on), and AITER's registered capture path raises on those instead of falling back (`mut_reg`). Copy-in adds nothing to the capture-time registration #57481 relies on (pr registered exactly base's graph-address counts) and costs one D2D memcpy node per captured gather.
- **Off switch:** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` or `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. Both also turn off AITER all-reduce; there is no gather-only switch. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` also keeps gathers on RCCL.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- **Scope.** The path runs on gfx950 and gfx942. End to end, only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash was measured: here on MI355X at TP4 `--monokernel` (c1-c32) and TP8 (c1-c4), and by the reviewer on MI325X (gfx942) at TP4 c1. Other models, MI350X (also gfx950) and MI300X (also gfx942) are unmeasured.
- **Copy-in leaves about 25 us per step on the table at c1** (M1/M2: -25 and -26 us; c2 within its rep range; c4 noise), matching the ~23 us the 5 captured copy-ins take per profiled step. Using the registered path for IPC-exportable inputs is a possible follow-up (see More detail).
- **Under the profiler, pr's TP4 step was slower** at c1 and c2 (8024 vs 6930 and 7913 vs 7180 us): its longer target-graph `hipGraphLaunch` call lands on the critical path once the profiler slows the host. Without the profiler, pr and r1 were faster in every run.
- **The margin narrows with size.** At the largest timed sizes the sweep gives 1.07-1.29x at TP2 and TP4 (16-20 MiB) and 1.31-2.45x at TP8 (8 MiB). At TP4 the target logits gather now stays on AITER up to 37 requests in flight and the draft logits gather up to 43 (4 and 5 with the old cap).
- **Dim 0 is measured only in isolation.** It becomes a copy plus a kernel instead of one RCCL kernel. It was faster at every timed size in at least one run (1.07-1.15x at 16-20 MiB); run 1 lost at 5 graph points of 128 KiB or less; none of DeepSeek-V4.1's decode gathers is dim 0. Int dtypes stay on RCCL: `all_gather_unreg` lacks the int-to-float view of AITER's `custom_all_gather` (a possible follow-up).

<details>
<summary>More detail and related PRs</summary>

- **Why no vLLM cap.** The previous head capped gathers at 2 MiB per rank (the CUDA custom all-gather default) until a sweep could set the cap. The two sweeps found no size, up to the timed maximum (TP2: 20 of 32 MiB), where RCCL won in both, so the cap is gone and `should_custom_ag`'s limit (vLLM's 128 MiB buffer / (2 x TP)) is the only size bound. Run 1 alone would have suggested 2 MiB at TP2 and 64 KiB at TP8 (see Sweep details). Prefill and sequence-parallel gathers under that limit now move to AITER too (for example 256 x 5120 bf16 at TP4: 1.18-1.19x under graph replay, 1.40-1.41x eager). Full 16k-token DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunks stay above it.
- **Copy-in cost, more.** With the eager logits gather's copy, which `mut_reg` keeps, the copy-ins take 29 us per profiled step. The registered-path follow-up needs all ranks to agree on the choice: exportability is per-rank allocator state, unlike the current shape-only gate. E1 did not probe exportability, and `mut_reg` was not run with expandable segments on DeepSeek-V4.1. `staged_rows` is allocated before the capture window, so it is the likely non-exportable input copy-in exists for.
- **The c4 logits gather, profiled.** At TP4 c4 the eager logits gather (1,809,920 B per rank) took 39.5 us for the AITER kernel plus 4.6 us for the copy-in, against 52.7 us for RCCL plus 10.0 us for `movedim` (rank 0).
- **`AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE=0` does not disable this path.** It turns off AITER all-reduce, but `should_custom_ag` does not read it. The DP path behaves the same way.
- **Concurrent streams.** AITER's all-gather and all-reduce share one pool and its signal slots, so TP collectives issued at the same time on two streams would race. This is already true of AITER all-reduce. Main has no such caller. The closest is the draft pure-TP DBO in #63483 (also carried in #63491), which gives its all-reduces their own per-microbatch NCCL communicators.
- **Not the `custom_all_gather` hook (#57856, #59730).** That hook gathers along dim 0 only, so the dim -1 logits gather would keep its `movedim` copy.
- **Complementary PRs:** #57856 and #61136 apply cleanly on top. #59730 (the CUDA counterpart, opt-in, draft) conflicts on one adjacent line in `__init__` (`use_aiter_tp_all_gather`), a trivial resolve. #60606's communicator hunk (the DCP group) applies cleanly; its `parallel_state.py` hunk conflicts with main already. #57832's int64 gathers keep their own helper.
- **PRs whose TP gathers will move to AITER on gfx950 and gfx942:** #59693, #63085, #63722 and #63723.
- **Sibling DeepSeek-V4.1 low-concurrency PRs.** They are independent of this one and share no files with it:
  - #63885 (build the SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950 with --monokernel)
  - #63888 (skip the top-k -1 fill on the rows vLLM's decode top-k writes)
  - #63891 (run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel)
  - #63892 (mono: batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late)
  - #63893 (mono: tuned K1 at TP4)

  On the earlier stack image (nightly 83c078d955 plus #63182, #63027, #63367, #63181 and #63355), the position-swapped stack of all six plus #63576 measured -9.5% at c1, less than the sum of the per-change gains, so changes that land later will show smaller increments.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Add fusions for Muse Glimmer for AMD backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview 1) Muse has a pattern rmsnorm + add + rmsnorm. This PR adds a fused kernel for these operations. Previously it had a single kernel that was from inductor but the custom AITER fused kernel has better perf (~2us / 40%) in decode and 30-40us / 50% in prefill. 2) Fuse the rmsnorm + reshape + rope and cache kernel. 3) (2) required AITER FA to be default. Baseline is using using vllm's ROCm FA backend which is not optimized. ## Claims TPOT and total tok/s should speed up substantially. ## Validation Concurrency | A TTFT ms | B TTFT ms | A TPOT ms | B TPOT ms | A total tok/s | B total tok/s -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | 60.4 | 57.2 | 13.5 | 11.0 | 147.5 | 181.9 2 | 88.2 | 98.4 | 14.0 | 11.3 | 283.6 | 350.5 4 | 162.1 | 162.1 | 15.0 | 11.5 | 526.9 | 688.7 8 | 290.0 | 294.3 | 16.4 | 12.6 | 958.2 | 1243.9 16 | 532.3 | 487.2 | 16.8 | 13.0 | 1846.3 | 2364.3 32 | 849.7 | 788.1 | 18.1 | 14.3 | 3379.8 | 4247.4 64 | 1388.2 | 1237.4 | 20.4 | 16.3 | 5888.8 | 7301.0 128 | 2125.1 | 1975.2 | 24.9 | 20.5 | 9462.5 | 11361.2 There should be a ~20% improvement in TPOT and total throughput (latter for decode heavy cases) and a ~5% improvement in TTFT. ## Details Fusions improve performance in decode by amortizing kernel launch latency. Moving to fused kernels improves decode performance and in some cases also TTFT. Before: The three kernels pre-attention are ~4us each (this is (1) from the Overview). The rmsnorm is 6us and is also ~30% larger in prefill (not in screenshot) most likely due to inductor not being great at generalizing for shapes (this is (2) from Overview). Attention is 144us (this is (3) from Overview). After: The fused kernel ((1)) is 4us (vs 12), rmsnorm is 4us (vs 6) and also ~30% faster and attention is 27us vs 144. There should be no changes to any backend other than ROCm. The changes are gated to both rocm and AITER being enabled. There is a new fusion pass added for the rmsnorm+add+rmsnorm as that did not exist before. Same with the qk rope pass. Unit tests are added for both. ---

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] DSpark: sliding-window MLA draft layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Extends DSpark speculative decoding with sliding-window MLA draft layers. Draft layers with an attention window now decode through the Triton MLA backend's windowed path, get a dedicated KV cache group, and can be driven by recurrent Markov heads whose state carries across the positions of one proposal. Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for DSpark / DCP / sliding-window work. Adjacent but distinct: #62410 (GLM-5.3 MLA DSpark drafts, model-specific enablement), #61464 (DBO with spec + DCP), #56694 / #62958 (Markov walk perf kernels). None cover windowed MLA draft layers, their KV cache layout, or the recurrent-head speculator hook. ## Claims - Triton MLA backend: sliding-window decode in both kernel stages. - Non-causal multi-token decode flag on the MLA KV cache spec and a separate KV cache group for windowed MLA draft layers. - Speculator hook for recurrent Markov heads that carry a state across the positions of one proposal. ## Validation - `python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py -v` — both extended by this change and wired into CI on CUDA. - The windowed decode path was exercised end-to-end during bring-up of the spec-decode stack this change originates from. ## Details - The windowed decode is implemented inside the Triton MLA kernel stages so a windowed draft layer costs no extra launches relative to the full-attention draft path. - The non-causal multi-token flag distinguishes speculative draft rows from target rows inside the same group, which is what lets windowed drafts share the MLA cache infrastructure instead of growing a parallel layout. - The recurrent Markov-head hook keeps proposal state out of the per-position interfaces: the speculator owns the state and re-enters the head per position.
