commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Support w4afp8 checkpoints on the W4A8 FP8 MoE path
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add a `w4afp8` quantization method so SGLang-style W4AFP8 MoE checkpoints (`PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8` and similar) load onto the existing compressed-tensors W4A8 FP8 MoE path from #58427. Load-time translation only: no kernel, model or `fused_moe` changes.

## Claims

- `w4afp8` checkpoints load and serve through `CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod` (Humming / CUTLASS W4A8) for routed experts and native FP8 block-128 for dense layers.
- The whole change is one new file (~100 lines) plus registration. The checkpoint layout is translated with `QuantizationConfig.get_checkpoint_weight_mapper()`, so the existing expert-params mapping and MoE method are used unchanged.
- Covers both input-scale namings seen on the Hub (`experts.N.w{1,2,3}.input_scale` and `experts.N.{gate,up,down}_proj.input_scale`) and both ignore-list keys (`modules_to_not_convert`, `ignored_layers`).

## Validation

Equivalence against the previous revision of this PR, which reported GSM8K 0.9113 on `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8` (8x H20, TP8+EP8): greedy decoding with top-5 logprobs on `nvcnvn/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-8L` (an 8-layer truncation of that checkpoint), 2x H200, TP2+EP2, `--enforce-eager --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, CUTLASS W4A8 MoE backend selected. Runs in order: new, old, new again.

| Comparison | Matching greedy tokens (4 prompts x 24) | Max abs logprob diff on shared prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| previous revision vs this revision (2nd run) | 96 / 96 | 5.5e-6 |
| this revision, 1st run vs 2nd run (same code) | 66 / 96 | 0.59 |

The first run after a fresh install diverges from both later runs by the same amount, so that gap is run-to-run noise in this setup, not this change. Weights load in ~7 s.

Load-time mapping on the real checkpoint index (CPU): all 4,608 routed-expert weights become int32 `weight_packed`, all 4,608 `weight_scale_inv` become `weight_scale`, all 4,608 `w{1,2,3}.input_scale` are dropped, and no non-expert tensor is touched.

<details><summary>Repro</summary>

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
llm = LLM("nvcnvn/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-8L", tensor_parallel_size=2, enable_expert_parallel=True,
          trust_remote_code=True, max_model_len=1024, enforce_eager=True,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, kv_cache_dtype="fp8_ds_mla")
llm.generate(["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):", "1 + 1 =", "请介绍一下你自己。"],
             SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24, logprobs=5))
```
</details>

Full-model GSM8K was not re-run for this revision; it requires the full checkpoint on 8 GPUs.

## Details

`W4AFP8Config` subclasses `Fp8Config`, so dense layers keep the native FP8 block-128 path. These checkpoints already store dense scales as `weight_scale_inv`, which is what that path expects. Routed experts are handed directly to `CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod`, with INT4 g128 symmetric weights and dynamic per-token FP8 activations.

The checkpoint mapper translates each routed-expert tensor before the model's loader sees it:

| On disk | Loaded as |
| --- | --- |
| `experts.N.*_proj.weight`: signed INT4, `int8`, 2 per byte | `*.weight_packed`: `uint4b8`, `int32`, 8 per word (XOR `0x88`, then `view(int32)`) |
| `experts.N.*_proj.weight_scale_inv` | `*.weight_scale` |
| `experts.N.*.input_scale` (static) | dropped: the W4A8 kernels quantize activations per token |

Limitations:
- **Group size and alignment:** group size must be 128, and hidden / per-partition intermediate sizes must be multiples of 256 (W4A8 method requirements).
- **MTP:** speculative decoding is not covered. MTP loaders such as `deepseek_mtp.py` are hand-written and do not apply the quant config's checkpoint mapper.
- **Out of scope:** `w4afp8_attnfp8` (Kimi-K3) is a different format and not handled here.

Supersedes the earlier revision of this PR, which added a custom MoE method subclass and an extra input-scale mapping in `routed_experts.py`. Prior attempts, #53848 and #49979, are closed.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Build][3/5] Speed up ROCm build: split the skinny GEMMs per kernel family and trim torch headers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` on one item - the kernel family (#15830 landed the file, #33762, #34304 and #40687 added kernels).**

`csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` holds four unrelated kernel families (LLMM1, wvSplitK, wvSplitKrc, wvSplitKQ) whose device code generation was serialized on one core (~58 s). Move the kernels to a header, give each family its own translation unit, and stop pulling `<torch/all.h>` into kernel headers.

`main` already contains #62475, so this PR is a single commit on top of it. Part of a 5-PR series with #62716 (paged attention), #62717 (topk softplus-sqrt), #63364 (int4 skinny GEMM) and #63365 (fused MUSE-Spark op); the gain is joint, see *Validation*. #62716 and #63364 have since landed in `main` and are merged into this branch, so the int4 unit is already split here.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 110 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 85 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1248 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Splits the skinny GEMM launchers per kernel family, so the four families compile in parallel instead of on one core; the largest unit drops from 58.3 s to 43.4 s.
- Trims `<torch/all.h>` from the launcher units: `rocm/quickreduce/custom_quickreduce.cu` goes from 30.4 s to 20.1 s.
- The skinny GEMMs stop being a straggler, which is what lets the attention and topk gains of the series show up in the wall clock.
- Nothing about what runs changes: 528 of the 534 launcher-body lines are byte-identical to the old file, no numerics change.

- The kernels and launchers are unchanged: 528 of the 534 launcher-body lines are byte-identical to the old file, and the 6 remaining lines are the two includes moved into `wvSplitKQ` plus the four workspace-pool constants moved into `wvSplitKrc`. No numerics change.
- The skinny GEMMs stop being a straggler, which is what lets the series' attention and topk gains show up in the wall clock.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 split the first (its tail drops to 448 s; that PR has landed) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail (now a `.cuh` plus one unit per `N_in`, after #63364) is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

| slowest unit per group, 1 arch (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |
| topk softplus-sqrt | not recorded | 99 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **1234 s / 8.7x** | **472 s / 25x** |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

| | MAX_JOBS=16 | MAX_JOBS=64 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main`, `f4edf9f0f0`) | 107 s | 85 s |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 92 s (−14 %) | 86 s (≈0 %) |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 107 s (≈0 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| **this PR** (`78a62ceb1c`) | **110 s (+3 %)** | **85 s (≈0 %)** |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | 109 s (+2 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | 108 s (+1 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`, `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=0`.

| check | configuration | result |
|---|---|---|
| moved code identity | scripted diff of the 4 launcher bodies and the header against `main` | 528 of 534 launcher-body lines byte-identical; header 1989 of 2035 lines byte-identical |
| `LLMM1` | fp16/bf16, M=16, K=4096 | rel. err 3e-3 (bf16) |
| `wvSplitK` / `wvSplitKrc` / `wvSplitKQ` vs torch matmul | fp16/bf16, k up to 4096, the N range each kernel supports (<=5, >=16, <=4) | rel. err 3e-4 (fp16), 3e-3 (bf16) |
| fresh configure + full build | from a clean tree | configure + build + link OK |

Repo tests for the kernels this PR touches:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py
```

`2519 passed, 636 skipped, 14 warnings in 223.85s (0:03:43)` — identical to `main` on the same host (`2519 passed, 636 skipped`).

The +1.1 MB is the per-family duplication of the now-inline helpers; sizes are RelWithDebInfo (debug info dominates).

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

The 9 release archs, one build at a time, same container and same command:

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | 1263 s | 266 MB |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 1261 s | 275 MB |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 1243 s | 269 MB |
| **this PR** (`78a62ceb1c`) | **1248 s** | **266 MB** |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | **600 s (−52 %)** | **257 MB** |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | **1241 s (−2 %)** | **266 MB** |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | **472 s (−63 %)** | **270 MB** |

At 9 archs the build is translation-unit-latency bound, not link bound: every host link is sub-second, while a handful of single units run for most of the wall (`skinny_gemms_int4.hip.o` alone is 1232 s of a 1234 s span). So a single PR does not move the 9-arch wall; that is expected, this PR's win is at 1 arch. It also does not make the 9-arch wheel any bigger. Pre-reland `main` (`db3b0f0fae`, i.e. #62475 without `--offload-compress`) fails this exact build with `mold: error: ... relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`, the failure #62983 reverted for.

## Details

Four kernel families with no code in common shared one translation unit, so `LLMM1` waited for `wvSplitKQ`'s device code generation and vice versa; the file was the second slowest unit of a ROCm build and became the slowest one as soon as the paged attention units were split.

The kernels and their shared helpers move to `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cuh`, and `skinny_gemms_{llmm1,wvsplitk,wvsplitkrc,wvsplitkq}.cu` each keep one host launcher. The five file-scope helpers (`get_lds_size`, `on_gfx1x`, `on_gfx12`, `on_gfx1151`, `mindiv`) become `inline` so the header can be included by several units, and CMake gains a single `VLLM_SKINNY_SRC` list used by the extension sources, by the `_rocm_C_skinny` object library and by the existing gfx1250 exclusion (which used to name the two files three times).

`<torch/all.h>` drags autograd, nn and jit into every kernel unit, and the header also included `rocm/dispatch_utils.h` - which includes `<torch/all.h>` itself - without using any of its FP8 dispatch macros. `skinny_gemms.cuh` now uses `<torch/types.h>` and no longer includes `dispatch_utils.h`; `skinny_gemms_wvsplitkq.cu` includes `dispatch_utils.h` (for `VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES`) and `quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cuh` (for `is_fp8_ocp()`) itself, and `custom_quickreduce.cu` switches to `<torch/types.h>`.

**Diagnostics change (the only one).** The arch-`#else` stubs in the header now `__builtin_trap()` instead of hitting a device `assert` with file/line (the old code `#undef`/`#define`d `NDEBUG` around `<assert.h>` to keep the assert live, which is order-dependent now that the file is a header). Those stubs are never launched - they exist so that the arch-specific `#if` in the launchers has something to call - so the difference only shows up if that invariant is ever violated.

**Naming and references.** The rename is followed through everywhere it leaks out of the build: the `.buildkite` `source_file_dependencies` entries that used to name `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` (which would have silently stopped triggering `test_rocm_gemm_rs_ar.py`) now list the new family units, and the `TORCH_CHECK` hint, the `vllm/` comments that point at the source (`layers/utils.py`, `v1/worker/utils.py`), the test comment and `torch_bindings.cpp` now name `skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu` / `skinny_gemms.cuh`. Those two lists are the only `.buildkite` change: the `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` entry stays as it was, so this PR does not change which int4 files trigger the step.

**Header hygiene.** `skinny_gemms.cuh` is now included by four units, so the pieces that used to be file-local were made safe for that: SPDX header, `#ifndef` guards around the `__HIP__GFX9__`/`__HIP__GFX1X__`/`__HIP__MI3XX__`/`LDS_SIZE` macros, `#undef LDS_SIZE` at the end of the header (the int4 unit defines its own, different value), `UNREACHABLE_CODE` is `__builtin_trap()` instead of an `#undef`/`#define NDEBUG` dance around `<assert.h>` (which used to depend on include order), and the inline helpers carry a note that their function-local statics are now one object per program rather than one per translation unit. `kWvSlots`/`kWvCaptureSlots` moved next to their only user, and the four launcher units keep a one-line header.

**How the file got this big.** Four PRs added kernels to `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu` (created by #15830), all in one TU:

| PR | landed | what it added |
|---|---|---|
| #15830 | 2025-04-21 | the file: 11 `__global__` kernels across the llmm1 / wvsplitk / wvsplitkrc / wvsplitkq families, 27 templates |
| #33762 | 2026-02-28 | 3 padded-stride kernel variants |
| #34304 | 2026-03-10 | 1 more kernel variant |
| #40687 | 2026-05-28 | the N=5 arm |

Arch support (#34709 for gfx1x, #40037 for gfx1102/gfx1103) multiplied those kernels by more targets without adding any, and the rest of the history (#33493, #34410, #34100, #40784, #56098, #60721) is tuning, workspace and header work. So 15 kernels ended up in one TU, which is why splitting by family is enough: they barely share code any more.

### Left to do

Follow-ups identified while doing this, deliberately out of scope:

- [ ] Guard the host-only ATen includes and launcher bodies with `__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__`: the device pass still parses them (10.5 s of the 43.4 s unit) although the kernels only need `c10::Half`/`BFloat16`/`Float8_e4m3fn`.
- [ ] Split `wvSplitk` by dtype: it is still the largest unit (43.4 s, of which ~32 s is codegen) and the frontend floor per unit is ~20 s, so the trade-off improved but did not disappear.
- [ ] `<torch/all.h>` still comes in via `rocm/dispatch_utils.h` for ~50 other TUs; trimming it there needs a CUDA build check.
- [ ] The `_rocm_C` extension holds `_rocm_C_skinny` as an object library; with the families split, giving each its own target would let `MAX_JOBS` scheduling prioritise the big ones.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: splitting `skinny_gemms.cuh` into a common header plus per-family kernel headers (the per-unit parse cost is real, ~20 s for the ~2000-line header, but it is unchanged by this PR and the split adds churn).
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: new tests (the existing `test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py` already covers all four families: 2519 passed, 636 skipped) and an execution run on gfx1100/gfx942 - a gfx1250-only configure and a gfx1030 compile were done instead.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Build][5/5] Speed up ROCm build: instantiate the fused MUSE-Spark op per head size
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits the fused MUSE-Spark op on one item - `head_dim` (64/128/256), the whole op having landed in #62132 five days ago.**

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` holds the whole fused MUSE-Spark qknorm/rope/kv-insert op: its host entry dispatches `head_dim` x `heads_per_group` x rope type, so 18 kernel instantiations land in a single translation unit. On a 9-arch build that unit is one of the longest compiles of the build - 478 s, behind only the int4 skinny GEMM (1232 s).

This PR instantiates one unit per `head_dim` (64/128/256): the kernels move into an include-only `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cuh` whose entry is a template over `HEAD_DIM`, each unit is two lines (`#include` + `VLLM_MUSE_SPARK_ENTRY(, hd)`), and `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_api.cu` keeps the public symbol and dispatches on `head_dim`, `extern template` keeping the device code in the three units.

Same kernels, same dispatch rules, same numerics: the only change is which translation unit generates which `head_dim`, plus the runtime forward in the API unit. At 1 arch the file is not the build's tail, so the single-arch wall is unchanged.

**This one only pays off once the int4 unit is split** (#63364): while that 1232 s unit exists it is the tail regardless of what this op costs, so on `main` alone this PR is expected to be neutral. The 9-arch numbers below are therefore measured on top of the int4 split.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 108 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 87 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1241 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Removes the second-longest compile of the 9-arch build (478 s, one unit) by instantiating one unit per `head_dim`: 3 units of the same total device code.
- Only pays off once the int4 unit is split; on `main` alone the 1232 s int4 unit stays the tail, so this PR is measured on top of #63364.
- Single-arch is unchanged within noise (107 -> 108 s at 16 jobs, 85 -> 87 s at 64).
- The op is not re-instantiated or reduced: each lane emits its `head_dim` arm's 18 configurations (2 dtypes x 3 heads_per_group x 2 rope types) exactly as before.
- One entry template with one explicit instantiation per `head_dim`, i.e. three distinct symbols; specialising a shared body by macro instead made the linker keep one copy and fail `head_dim` 128/256 at runtime.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 splits the first (its tail drops to 448 s) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

| slowest unit per group, 1 arch (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |
| topk softplus-sqrt | not recorded | 99 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **1234 s / 8.7x** | **472 s / 25x** |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

 gfx950, cold builds in the same container:

| build | `MAX_JOBS=16` | `MAX_JOBS=64` |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main`, `f4edf9f0f0`) | 107 s | 85 s |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 92 s (−14 %) | 86 s (≈0 %) |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 107 s (≈0 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 110 s (+3 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | 109 s (+2 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| **this PR** (`31de254fe4`) | 108 s (+1 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | **1263 s** | **266 MB** |
| #62716 paged attention 089bbaf68a | 1261 s | 275 MB |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 1243 s | 269 MB |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 1248 s | 266 MB |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | **600 s (−52 %)** | **257 MB** |
| **this PR** (`31de254fe4`) | **1241 s (−2 %)** | **266 MB** |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | **472 s (−63 %)** | **270 MB** |

Per-unit detail at this configuration:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| MUSE-Spark unit | 478 s, one unit | 3 units of the same total device code |
| `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_api.cu` | - | 27 lines, no device code |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, clang 23, mold.

Structure check on the 9-arch objects: the API unit emits 0 device kernel symbols and each of the three lane units 240 - i.e. each unit instantiates only its own `head_dim`.

#### Linked artifact sizes at 9 archs

Context for these: [#62983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62983) had to revert #62475 because the 9-arch `_rocm_C.abi3.so` outgrew the 2 GiB reach of the 32-bit PC-relative relocations in `crtbegin`'s `.text` (plain `main` was already at 2011.5 MiB, and the 12-way split added ~119 MiB of duplicated GPU debug info, overflowing at 2104 MiB). `--offload-compress`, which landed with the reland (#63105), shrinks the fatbin ~20x and is what keeps us away from that wall.

| linked artifact (9 archs) | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` | TBD | **125.9 MB** | **129.3 MB** |
| `_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` | TBD | **499.8 MB** | **499.8 MB** |
| `_moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` | TBD | **235.2 MB** | **239.8 MB** |
| `_C.abi3.so` | TBD | **30.7 MB** | **30.0 MB** |
| `.o` files under `CMakeFiles/` | TBD | **935 MB** | **932 MB** |

The split does not add device code - it moves the same `head_dim` arm's kernels into different units - so the 9-arch `_rocm_C` stays where `main` puts it, and across the five PRs the wheel is about the same size (266 -> 270 MB).

### Runtime check

The existing kernel test file covers `head_dim` 64/128/256 through the public entry, i.e. through the new forward, and was run on both builds of `bdc0f947` (each a fresh `MAX_JOBS=64 pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation`; the later `main` merge does not touch these files):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py
```

```
29 passed, 2 skipped in 15.74s      # CUDA, 8x H100, cu134 nightly
26 passed, 5 deselected in 10.01s   # ROCm, MI350X/gfx950, -k "not attention_metadata"
```

The 2 CUDA skips are ROCm-only cases (backend gate, compile boundary). The 5 ROCm deselects are `test_query_fusion_respects_attention_metadata`, which import `flashinfer` and were absent from that container only; they are among the 29 that pass on CUDA. The split builds and runs on both paths, and each `head_dim` gets its own `..._typed<hd>` instantiation.

## Details

The kernel is untouched: the `__global__` template and the `DISPATCH_ARGS`/`DISPATCH_HPG`/`DISPATCH_ROPE_T` tower are unchanged. What changed is how the `head_dim` arm is selected - `HEAD_DIM` is a template parameter of `launchFusedMuseSpark`, so the runtime `switch (head_dim)` is a single `DISPATCH_ROPE_T(HEAD_DIM)` and each unit's symbols carry their own head_dim - plus the API unit dispatching to `..._typed<64/128/256>`. A `head_dim` outside 64/128/256 still reports "unsupported head_dim".

**How the file got this big.** It has no growth history: #62132 landed the whole op five days ago, in one TU, as 1 `__global__` with 8 templates and `head_dim` {64,128,256} x `heads_per_group` {1,2,4} x rope type {fp32, scalar_t} - 18 configurations per dtype pair, plus the fp8-output arms. Nothing has been added to it since.

So its 478 s at 9 archs is the cost of that configuration set on day one, not of accretion; this PR splits it into 3 units.

### Left to do

- [ ] Cross-check with #63364: this branch is based on `main`, so its 9-arch numbers are taken with the int4 split merged in; on `main` alone the change is neutral (1241 s vs 1263 s).
- [x] Run `tests/kernels/test_fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` on this revision (it covers head_dim 64/128/256 through the public entry, i.e. through the new forward). Done, see *Runtime check*.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix DP ViT all-gather dtype mismatch when the first parameter is fp32
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, ranks that get no images all-gather placeholder embeddings whose dtype comes from `next(vision_model.parameters())`. Since #64111, MiniMax-M3 keeps its patch embedding in fp32 while the tower outputs bf16. Ranks with images then gather bf16 and ranks without gather fp32, so the all-gather mismatches and startup hangs.

This uses the vision model's `dtype` attribute when it has one, and falls back to the first parameter's dtype otherwise. Other models are unchanged: their `dtype` either matches the first parameter or isn't defined.

## Test plan

- `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` with `-tp 4 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data` now starts and serves image requests. Before the fix, it hung after the encoder profile run.
- Ongoing coverage comes from the nightly MiniMax-M3 evals, which run with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Re-fit `--max-model-len auto` after the extensible KV cache shrinks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (default on CUDA/ROCm with model runner V2, #56492), `--max-model-len auto` is fitted at planning time, against a budget that leaves out CUDA graphs and warmup on purpose: the KV cache is committed later, from the memory measured after warmup. When that measurement can no longer hold the fitted length, `finalize_extensible_kv_cache` only checks it and startup fails, even though the user never asked for that length. This PR fits the length again to the measured capacity, for `auto` only.

## Claims

- `--max-model-len auto` no longer fails at startup when CUDA graphs and warmup leave less KV cache than the planning-time fit assumed. It starts at the longest length that fits the measured capacity and logs the reduction.
- No change for any configuration that starts today:
  - An explicit `--max-model-len` that does not fit still fails, as before.
  - For `auto`, the re-fit searches only lengths at or below the current one, so when the measured capacity holds the current length, it is kept and nothing else happens.
- +24 lines: `kv_cache_planning.py` +19, `engine/core.py` +5. Plus one unit test.

## Validation

**Unit test:** `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_refits_auto_max_model_len`. It fails without the fix (startup `ValueError`) and passes with it. The whole file passes: 66 passed. Pre-commit passes.

**Reproducer on GB200 (4x GPU, TP4), on main alone.** The model is MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4-DFlash with the command from `docs/features/speculative_decoding/adaptive_verification.md`, adaptive verification off. Both trees are main `254a2a3390`; the PR tree adds this fix. CUDA graphs take 3.93 GiB in every run, and the full 1,048,576-token context needs 15.06 GiB of KV cache.

| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | KV budget at planning (`auto` keeps 1,048,576) | KV measured after warmup | main | this PR: `max_model_len` from `/v1/models` | GSM8K, 1319 questions, C256 (main → this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 (default) | 42.26 GiB | 23.09 GiB | starts at 1,048,576 | 1,048,576, unchanged | 94.77% → 94.62% |
| 0.93 | | 17.76 GiB | starts at 1,048,576 | 1,048,576, unchanged | 94.39% → 94.62% |
| 0.90 | 24.33 GiB | 12.24 GiB | **fails**: `ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (1048576), (15.06 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (12.24 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 812064.` | **starts at 812,064**, the length main's own error suggests | fails → 95.07% |

The same failure happens at the default utilization whenever graphs or warmup take more memory. With the wider CUDA graphs of #63406, about 12.7 GiB of KV cache is left, and main fails the same way. With this fix on top, the server starts at 846,480 tokens and scores 94.24% on GSM8K at C256 and at C1024.

## Details

Root cause: under the extensible KV cache, `profile_cudagraph_memory` returns 0, because the capture footprint is measured after warmup rather than estimated. That is right for sizing the KV cache, but `auto` still picks its length from the pre-capture budget. `finalize_extensible_kv_cache` then commits the measured block count, and `shrink_kv_cache_configs` raises if one request of `max_model_len` no longer fits.

The fix calls the planning-time `_auto_fit_max_model_len` again, with the measured block count and the same bytes-per-block and null-block accounting that `shrink_kv_cache_configs` checks. If the length changes, the engine core syncs it to the workers with the existing `update_max_model_len`, as the planning-time auto-fit already does.

Shrinking after capture is safe: buffers sized from the planning-time length, such as block tables, still cover a shorter one. Moving the whole `auto` decision after warmup is not an option, because block tables, warmup steps and drafters need a length before capture.

The extensible KV cache is only enabled with model runner V2, so model runner V1 is unaffected.

commits.pr_title: [GLM 5.3 Perf] Expand fp8 moe tma for sm100, 1.03~1.60x kernel performance improvement
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow up for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63820

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Compare Triton pointer and B-TMA loads for a GLM-5.3 local FP8 MoE shard.

Run from the repository root with ``PYTHONPATH=.``. Routing is precomputed;
the timings cover the local MoE kernels, not model serving.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import replace
from functools import partial
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
import triton.testing
from triton.tools.tensor_descriptor import TensorDescriptor

from tests.kernels.moe.utils import (
    make_dummy_moe_config,
    make_test_quant_config,
    modular_triton_fused_moe,
)
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import override_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import try_get_optimal_moe_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
    fused_topk_bias,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager, reset_workspace_manager

TOKENS = (1, 8, 32, 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 8192)
EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTERMEDIATE, TOPK = 256, 6144, 2048, 8


def run(kernel, config, x, w1, w2, weights, ids, use_tma):
    with override_config({**config, "USE_TMA": use_tma}):
        return kernel.apply(
            x,
            w1,
            w2,
            weights,
            ids,
            activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
            global_num_experts=EXPERTS,
            expert_map=None,
            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
        )


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--tp", type=int, choices=(4, 8), default=4)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    n = INTERMEDIATE // args.tp

    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
    torch.manual_seed(123)
    init_workspace_manager(torch.device(0))
    try:
        with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.inference_mode():
            w1, w2, quant = make_test_quant_config(
                EXPERTS,
                n,
                HIDDEN,
                torch.bfloat16,
                torch.float8_e4m3fn,
                block_shape=[128, 128],
            )
            print(f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name()} GLM-5.3 TP={args.tp}")
            print("tokens pointer_us b_tma_us speedup", flush=True)
            for m in TOKENS:
                x = (torch.randn(m, HIDDEN) / 10).to(torch.bfloat16)
                logits = torch.randn(m, EXPERTS, dtype=torch.float32)
                bias = torch.randn(EXPERTS, dtype=torch.float32) / 10
                weights, ids = fused_topk_bias(
                    x,
                    logits,
                    "sigmoid",
                    bias,
                    TOPK,
                    True,
                    routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
                )
                moe = make_dummy_moe_config(
                    num_experts=EXPERTS,
                    experts_per_token=TOPK,
                    hidden_dim=HIDDEN,
                    intermediate_size=INTERMEDIATE,
                    max_num_tokens=m,
                )
                moe.moe_parallel_config = replace(
                    moe.moe_parallel_config, tp_size=args.tp
                )
                moe.intermediate_size_per_partition = n
                kernel = modular_triton_fused_moe(moe, quant)
                config = try_get_optimal_moe_config(
                    w1.shape,
                    w2.shape,
                    TOPK,
                    "fp8_w8a8",
                    m,
                    block_shape=[128, 128],
                )
                call = partial(run, kernel, config, x, w1, w2, weights, ids)

                pointer = call(False)
                with patch.object(
                    TensorDescriptor, "from_tensor", wraps=TensorDescriptor.from_tensor
                ) as descriptors:
                    tma = call(True)
                assert len(descriptors.call_args_list) == 2
                assert all(c.args[0].ndim == 3 for c in descriptors.call_args_list)
                torch.testing.assert_close(pointer, tma, atol=0, rtol=0)

                pointer_us = 1000 * triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
                    partial(call, False), rep=100
                )
                tma_us = 1000 * triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
                    partial(call, True), rep=100
                )
                print(
                    f"{m:>6} {pointer_us:>10.1f} {tma_us:>8.1f} "
                    f"{pointer_us / tma_us:>7.2f}x",
                    flush=True,
                )
    finally:
        reset_workspace_manager()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

And we can get

## Overview Raise patched dependency floors for file locking, telemetry, GraphQL and test/documentation tools, then regenerate all four platform test locks and the documentation lock. This follows #62835 and targets 126 alert instances in the audited dependency snapshot; individual advisories appear in multiple requirement files. ## Claims | Dependency | Minimum / locked version | | --- | --- | | filelock | 4.2.4 | | virtualenv | 21.14.13 | | graphql-core | >=3.2.12,<3.3; locked to 3.2.13 | | OpenTelemetry API, SDK and OTLP exporters | 1.45.1 | | nltk | 3.10.4 | | black | 26.10.1 | | GitPython | 3.2.1 | - Update source floors so regeneration retains the patched versions. Keep GraphQL within the existing 3.2 release line and align the telemetry package family. - Preserve unrelated pins. Supporting changes are limited to virtualenv dependencies, telemetry dependencies and removal of packages no longer required by telemetry. ## Validation - All five locks regenerated successfully with uv 0.11.1 and their checked-in platform/backend/constraint/exclusion arguments. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. - Existing vLLM tracing suite: **3 passed** with OpenTelemetry 1.45.1 and a local collector. - Standalone local compatibility checks: **9 passed** for model-cache locking, virtualenv creation, NLTK model persistence, GraphQL parsing/execution, GitPython repository operations and Black formatting. The script is included below for reproduction and is not added to the repository. - The three NLTK outside-root read/write and GraphQL comment-token-budget checks failed on the old nltk 3.10.3 / graphql-core 3.2.6 versions (`DID NOT RAISE`) and passed with the upgraded versions. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files requirements/common.txt requirements/docs.in requirements/docs.txt requirements/test/cpu.txt requirements/test/cuda.in requirements/test/cuda.txt requirements/test/rocm.in requirements/test/rocm.txt requirements/test/xpu.in requirements/test/xpu.txt PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tracing tests/tracing/test_loading_tracing.py -q PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_dependency_compatibility.py --basetemp=/tmp/vllm-dependency-checks -q ``` The checks ran on macOS with Python 3.12 and the listed target package versions. **Not run:** Linux GPU/ROCm/XPU runtime integration, full serving/model evaluations or a full rendered documentation build. Platform lock resolution and local checks do not establish hardware compatibility; those validations remain pending.
Standalone local compatibility checks Save as `/tmp/test_dependency_compatibility.py` and run the command above in an environment with the upgraded packages. The before-change reproduction used a separate package directory containing only nltk 3.10.3 and graphql-core 3.2.6, prepended to `PYTHONPATH`, and selected `-k 'rejects_outside_model or comment_token_budget'`: **3 failed, 6 deselected**. With the upgraded packages the full script reported **9 passed**. Use a shared `/tmp` location for `--basetemp`: NLTK explicitly trusts private per-user temporary directories on macOS. ```python import json import subprocess from pathlib import Path import pytest @pytest.fixture def nltk_root(tmp_path, monkeypatch): import nltk import nltk.pathsec allowed = tmp_path / 'allowed' allowed.mkdir(mode=0o700) old_paths = list(nltk.data.path) nltk.data.path[:] = [str(allowed)] monkeypatch.setenv('NLTK_DATA', str(allowed)) assert nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE try: yield allowed, tmp_path finally: nltk.data.path[:] = old_paths def test_nltk_rejects_outside_model_write(nltk_root): from nltk.tag.perceptron import AveragedPerceptron _, root = nltk_root target = root / 'outside.json' with pytest.raises(PermissionError): AveragedPerceptron().save(str(target)) assert not target.exists() def test_nltk_rejects_outside_model_read(nltk_root): from nltk.tag.perceptron import AveragedPerceptron _, root = nltk_root target = root / 'outside.json' target.write_text(json.dumps({'feature': {'NN': 1.0}})) with pytest.raises(PermissionError): AveragedPerceptron().load(str(target)) def test_nltk_allowed_model_roundtrip(nltk_root): from nltk.tag.perceptron import AveragedPerceptron from nltk.stem import PorterStemmer allowed, _ = nltk_root target = allowed / 'weights.json' model = AveragedPerceptron() model.weights = {'feature': {'NN': 1.0}} model.save(str(target)) loaded = AveragedPerceptron() loaded.load(str(target)) assert loaded.weights == model.weights assert PorterStemmer().stem('running') == 'run' def test_graphql_comment_token_budget(): from graphql import GraphQLError, parse with pytest.raises(GraphQLError, match='more than 10 tokens'): parse('{\n' + '# comment\n' * 1000 + 'field\n}', max_tokens=10) def test_graphql_normal_query(): from graphql import build_schema, graphql_sync schema = build_schema('type Query { greeting: String! }') result = graphql_sync(schema, '{ greeting }', root_value={'greeting': 'hello'}) assert result.errors is None assert result.data == {'greeting': 'hello'} def test_vllm_model_cache_lock_contention(tmp_path): from filelock import Timeout from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import get_lock first = get_lock('test/model', cache_dir=str(tmp_path)) second = get_lock('test/model', cache_dir=str(tmp_path)) assert first.lock_file == second.lock_file assert first.mode == 0o666 with first: with pytest.raises(Timeout): second.acquire(timeout=0.05) with second.acquire(timeout=1): assert second.is_locked def test_virtualenv_creation_without_seeding(tmp_path): from virtualenv import cli_run target = tmp_path / '.venv' cli_run(['--no-seed', str(target)], setup_logging=False) result = subprocess.run([str(target / 'bin/python'), '-c', 'import sys; print(sys.prefix)'], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True) assert Path(result.stdout.strip()).resolve() == target.resolve() assert (target / 'pyvenv.cfg').exists() def test_gitpython_local_repository(tmp_path): from git import Actor, Repo repo = Repo.init(tmp_path / 'repo') content = Path(repo.working_tree_dir) / 'example.txt' content.write_text('dependency check\n') repo.index.add(['example.txt']) actor = Actor('Dependency Check', 'dependency-check@example.invalid') commit = repo.index.commit('Local validation', author=actor, committer=actor) assert repo.head.commit.hexsha == commit.hexsha assert repo.git.show('HEAD:example.txt') == 'dependency check' assert not repo.is_dirty() def test_black_basic_formatting(): import black assert black.format_str('value=1\n', mode=black.Mode()) == 'value = 1\n' ```

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Avoid importing humming when resolving quantization configs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Resolving any quantized model's config imports `humming` in the front-end process, even for checkpoints that never use it (e.g. plain FP8). Importing `humming` starts two background build helper processes. This PR makes `utils/humming/schema.py` build its dtype tables lazily, so nothing imports `humming` until a Humming layer actually needs it.

Related: vllm-project/humming#184 skips those helpers when precompiled wheel artifacts are present. This change keeps vLLM from importing `humming` at all in processes that don't use it.

## Claims

- `get_quantization_config(...)` no longer imports `humming` for any quantization method. On current main it does for all of them, leaving 2 helper processes running in the importing process.
- No behavior change on Humming paths: the same dtype tables are built on first use and cached.

## Validation

Before vs. after, resolving `fp8`, `gptq`, `awq`, `compressed-tensors`, `modelopt_fp4`, and `mxfp4` configs:

| | `humming` in `sys.modules` | Humming helper child processes |
|---|---|---|
| main | True | 2 |
| this PR | False | 0 |

Reproduce:
```python
import sys
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import get_quantization_config
get_quantization_config("fp8")
print("humming" in sys.modules)  # main: True, this PR: False
```

Tests on H200 with humming installed:
```
pytest tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_compile.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py tests/config/test_config_generation.py
84 passed, 4 skipped
```

I also directly exercised all four rewritten functions (`weight_schema_to_quant_key`, `input_schema_to_quant_key`, `quant_key_to_input_schema`, `check_and_fallback_input_schema`) and the `moe.py` caller.

I did not add a regression test. It would belong in `tests/quantization`, whose CI job is currently disabled pending the torchao pin; the snippet above checks it.

## Details

The import chain is:

1. `get_quantization_config()` imports every quantization config.
2. Quark's MoE config imports `fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py`, which imports the `utils/humming` package.
3. That package imports `schema.py`, which calls `if has_humming():` at module level.
4. `has_humming()` trial-imports the package rather than only checking `find_spec`.

The two module-level tables become `functools.cache` getters. The two functions that used the module-global `humming_dtypes` now import it locally, next to the `vllm.utils.humming` imports they already had. Workers that actually run Humming layers still import it (and its helpers) as before.

This was found while profiling Humming JIT compile time during vLLM startup.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Treat standalone draft model prefill as decode
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its draft prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds the correction token sampled by the target. `max_decode_query_len()` returns `1 + num_speculative_tokens`, so every spec-as-decode attention builder sets its reorder threshold one token short. Each draft-prefill request is classified as a **prefill**, and the FULL graph captures the backend's prefill path.

That has two consequences:
- **Correctness:** `UNIFORM_BATCH` backends only promise FULL-graph safety for uniform *decode* batches. FlashInfer's TRTLLM prefill path was not graph-safe, which caused the GB200 crash reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731. #65598 fixed that specific allocation, but the prefill path is still outside what `UNIFORM_BATCH` covers.
- **Performance:** the draft prefill runs the prefill attention kernel even though it is decode-shaped.

On model runner V2, this PR makes `max_decode_query_len()` add `speculative_config.max_num_new_slots_for_drafting`, the extra per-request slots the drafter adds. The scheduler already reserves this same quantity in its input budget. It is 1 for the standalone draft model and 0 for every other V2 method. V2 rejects `parallel_drafting` for everything except DFlash and DSpark, which report 0. Spec-as-decode builders now classify the `K + 2` draft prefill as a decode, and the reorder threshold, varlen CUDA graph bounds and other readers of `max_decode_query_len()` stay consistent because they all read the same function. The V1 parallel-drafting branch is unchanged and is now an `elif`, so the two adjustments can never stack.

Effects on the target model: with the standalone draft model, the target's spec-as-decode builders also get a threshold of `K + 2`, so target prompt tails of exactly `K + 2` tokens use the decode kernels, as tails of `K + 1` or fewer tokens already do. GSM8K results below are unchanged for a dense and a hybrid target.

## Test Plan

All runs on 1x GB200 with model runner V2. Target `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, draft `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, default attention backend (FlashInfer). The benchmarks used an equivalent version of this change: two separate `if` blocks instead of `if/elif`, with identical logic.

1. **Decode path.** Builder thresholds inspected in a running engine through `collective_rpc`, and an nsys profile (`--cuda-graph-trace=node`) of 64 SPEED-Bench prompts × 256 tokens on `main` (7ecc83a987) vs this PR.
2. **Performance.** `vllm bench serve` on SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k` (about 1.9k-token prompts), `--speed-bench-output-len 2048 --ignore-eos`, `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 256`, concurrency 1/16/64/256, two runs per side in main → PR → PR → main order on the same GPU.
3. **Accuracy.** GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, greedy) at concurrency 256 and 32. Run on 947bd30e0b, before #65598 merged.

**Builder thresholds** (target / draft): `main` 4 / 4, this PR 5 / 5.

**Attention kernels inside the CUDA graphs** (nsys):

| | TRTLLM prefill (`...PersistentContext`) | TRTLLM decode (`...ForGen`) | Attention GPU time |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4172 launches, 754.9 ms | 12852 launches, 772.8 ms | 1527.7 ms |
| this PR | 448 launches, 133.7 ms | 16560 launches, 1009.0 ms | 1142.7 ms (−25%) |

About 3700 draft-prefill launches move from the prefill kernel to the decode kernel, and the 448 prefill launches that remain are real prompt prefills.

**SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k`** (mean of 2 runs per side):

| Concurrency | Throughput main (tok/s) | Throughput PR | Δ | Mean TPOT main (ms) | Mean TPOT PR | Δ | Accepted/draft main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 299 | 326 | +9.2% | 3.33 | 3.05 | −8.4% | 1.62 / 1.68 |
| 16 | 3402 | 3766 | +10.7% | 4.43 | 3.99 | −9.9% | 1.68 / 1.66 |
| 64 | 6858 | 8203 | +19.6% | 8.51 | 7.15 | −16.0% | 1.74 / 1.71 |
| 256 | 8367 | 10860 | +29.8% | 27.65 | 21.21 | −23.3% | 1.74 / 1.72 |

**GSM8K** (accuracy, accepted tokens per draft):

| Target | main (pre-#65598) | this PR | main, `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (reference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B, concurrency 256 | crash (illegal memory access) | 0.886, 2.447 | 0.887, 2.445 |
| Qwen3-8B, concurrency 32 | — | 0.886, 2.437 | 0.886, 2.436 |

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf] Fused GDN MTP: Support DSpark K=8 and use idle SMs at small batch sizes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This PR makes two changes to the fused GDN MTP decode kernel: 1. **K=8 support:** DSpark K=8 (9 tokens per request) fell back to the slower Triton path. The kernel now handles 9 tokens. Overlaps with #53070. 2. **Split-V:** at small batch sizes, each value head is split over a cluster of 2 or 4 thread blocks to use idle SMs (SM90+). With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and DSpark K=8, this PR increases output throughput over main by 18% on B300 and 13% on H100 with a single request. With 8 or more concurrent requests, the gain is 6% to 9% on B300 (measured up to 128 requests) and 2% to 6% on H100 (measured up to 32 requests). ## Claims - DSpark K=8 decode steps now use the fused kernel. On main they silently fall back to the Triton delta-rule + gated RMSNorm path in every GDN layer, because the kernel accepts at most 8 tokens. - The cluster split (SM90+) cuts the fused kernel time at 1 request from 22.3µs to 10.2µs on B300 and from 26.2µs to 14.3µs on H100. From 8 requests on, where it does not split, the kernel is 0.4% to 0.9% faster. It also speeds up K=7 by 8% at c1, which already used the fused kernel. - MTP3 does not regress: output throughput rises 2% to 3% at c1 and c2, and matches main from c4 on. - Outputs unchanged: GSM8K and acceptance length match main. ## E2E Benchmarks Serving benchmark. main is `5225a1f17f` (main on 2026-11-04), and this PR is based on it. B300 uses the bf16 model, H100 uses `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (bf16 does not fit): ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8}' ``` Client: AIPerf 0.13, config and command below. Output tok/s is measured over the steady window, which opens once the first c requests complete. Every reported point passed the validity checks (no errors, preemptions or queueing, server saturated).

The new 4- and 16-request cases cover the split=2 and split=1 paths. The existing cases have at most 3 requests, so they always split on B300 and H100. In CI, `kernels/fla` runs on B200 and `kernels/mamba` on H200 MIG, so both exercise the split path. ## Details **9 tokens.** DSpark K=8 verifies 8 drafts plus the bonus token, so `state_indices` has width 9 and `_can_use_fused_gdn_mtp_decode` rejected it. Raising `kMaxMtpTokens` alone is not enough: the kernel assigned one warp per token and has 8 warps, so the 9th token was skipped. Warps now stride over tokens. Static shared memory at 9 tokens with fp32 state is ~45.6KB, under the 48KB static limit. **Related work.** - #53070 adds the same 9-token support as a separate width-9 template specialization next to the width-8 one. It has had no activity since Aug 31 and predates the move of the kernel to `csrc/gdn/`. This PR raises the cap in place instead (one kernel, warps stride over tokens). The cluster split does not depend on how the 9-token support lands, so it can be rebased onto #53070 if that one is preferred. - benchislett/vllm#8 (draft) extends fused GDN verification to 12 and 16 tokens (K=11 and K=15) on SM107, with a separate wide kernel that is used when the width exceeds `kMaxMtpTokens`. It complements this PR: with both, 9 tokens would use the kernel changed here and 12 or 16 tokens the wide kernel. - #54612 speeds up the Triton spec-decode recurrence for Qwen3-Next, which is the path that DSpark K=8 falls back to on main. This PR moves K=8 off that path to the fused CUDA kernel. **Cluster split.** At small batch sizes the kernel launches one CTA per (request, value head), e.g. 32 CTAs on 148 SMs at batch size 1. On SM90+, each head's V rows are split over a cluster of 2 or 4 CTAs (`blockIdx.z`) while the grid still fits in one wave at 2 CTAs per SM. Each CTA loads and updates its slice of the state. The gated RMSNorm sums the partial sums of squares of the cluster through distributed shared memory, with a final cluster barrier so no CTA exits while others read its shared memory. Without a split, the kernel keeps its single-pass epilogue, so batch sizes of 8 and more are unchanged. On B300 and H100 (HV=32) the split is 4 up to 2 requests, 2 at 4 requests, 1 from 8 requests. **Tradeoffs and limitations.** - The split choice is a host-side heuristic from the SM count, no tuning table. It queries two device attributes on the host per launch, with no GPU sync. - SM80 to SM89 never split. There, the split kernels compile to a trap stub to keep them out of the binary. - Validated on B300 and H100 only. SM100 and SM120 take the same path but were not tested. - Each kernel instantiation now has three split variants. Compiling this file for all 7 target archs (one nvcc 13.0 call with `--compress-mode=size`) takes 71s instead of 36s, and the object grows from 0.41MB to 0.90MB. - Mixed prefill and decode batches still use the unfused path, as before. They are CUDA graphed on main. CC @Jie-Fang @ZJY0516 @gau-nernst @vadiklyutiy @benchislett @BabyDrangoner 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2]  Read routed experts from unkeyed full blocks
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix routed-expert output reconstruction after a prefix-cache hit when EAGLE/MTP lookahead hashing leaves a complete block without a key. Read request-local pending blocks alongside the incomplete tail.

Related: [[#61589 — Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589).

## Claims

- Handle output ranges spanning published blocks, pending full blocks, and an incomplete tail.
- Return an independent array that remains valid after buffer reuse.
- Add buffer, worker, and `LLM` regression coverage, with auxiliary-output changes triggering the existing speculative-decoding CI jobs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py -q
```
**81 passed, 14 warnings in 13.82s.**

## Details

Lookahead hashing requires the token after a block before its hash can be generated. Routing rows can therefore form a complete block while still waiting in `pending_blocks`.

For a 48-token prompt with block size 16:

1. A cold request computes `[0,48)` and returns its current rows directly.
2. A subsequent request reuses `[0,32)` and recomputes `[32,48)`.
3. The recomputed block is complete, but its hash depends on the new request's first generated token at position 48.
4. Output reconstruction reads `[0,32)` from the store, then needs the pending `[32,48)` block. The old `read()` only checked the incomplete tail, which does not exist here, and asserted.

The fix passes pending blocks to `RoutedExpertsBuffer.read()` and combines them with the tail to cover the requested interval. It retains the coverage assertion and copies the output. Reading leaves pending blocks available for publication when their hashes arrive.
